column1: Latest email engagement is not classified correctly on Lead and Contact
column2:
CONTEXT
Sales teams need the latest email date, direction, and body visible on each Lead or Contact. Native messages and email Tasks are processed through separate flows.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Inbound replies logged as Tasks are stamped as sent emails, making the latest engagement state unreliable.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The newest relevant email should update the person record as Email Sent or Email Reply without older messages overwriting newer activity.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The Task flow classified every email as Email Sent because Task has no Incoming field. Subject prefixes also proved inconsistent.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Native email direction is reliable through Incoming and EmailMessageRelation. In a labelled Task sample, outbound sales-engagement emails consistently contained a tracking prefix in Description, while inbound messages did not.

RESOLUTION
Separate bulk-safe flows were implemented. Native emails use Incoming and relation type; Tasks use the verified Description prefix. A date guard prevents stale overwrites, and the backfill keeps only the newest engagement.

VALIDATION
The Task rule classified all 30 labelled samples correctly. Lead and Contact scenarios, stale dates, missing relations, and a bulk load of approximately 200 messages were tested without limit errors.

column1: Hebrew natural-language questions generate incorrect or invalid SOQL
column2:
CONTEXT
A Salesforce dashboard translates Hebrew questions into SOQL and presents answers as tables or charts. The schema contains managed-package objects and ambiguous business terms.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Common questions about claims, agents, products, and conversion rates return errors or semantically incorrect results.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Questions should map to the correct schema, filters, and aggregation rules. Raw record queries should render as tables, and unsupported requests should be rejected safely.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The model confused claims with service requests, used fields on the wrong object, grouped by nonexistent relationships, returned IDs instead of names, and produced invalid aliases.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The failures came from incomplete schema grounding, contradictory prompt rules, ambiguous terminology, and missing business definitions.

RESOLUTION
The prompt and schema map were revised with verified relationships, picklists, business rules, SOQL examples, a fallback, column controls, and table routing. This is partial because roughly 150 questions remain.

VALIDATION
The original failing questions now produce valid queries and expected live-data results. Schema and prompt rules were reviewed through three correction rounds, but final acceptance depends on completing the remaining question set.

column1: Credits and contract conversions need a traceable many-to-many process
column2:
CONTEXT
A Salesforce process handles refunds and conversions of unused contract value. The manual process could not reliably support partial actions, multiple sources and targets, or a complete audit trail.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Users need a money-pool workflow that balances source value against new contracts while preserving history.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Selected contracts should contribute value into one pool, allocations should balance before commit, and every source and target should remain traceable. Refunds must exclude bonus quantities and apply agreed fees and tax.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The one-to-one model required multi-step conversions, overwrote history, and could not represent non-lead budgets. New target contracts also require values that cannot be inherited logically.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
A Screen Flow was selected to reduce maintenance. Testing identified open decisions for required target fields and validation messages.

RESOLUTION
Version 34 implements source selection, pool accumulation, allocation, a hard balance gate, audit objects, deductions, and refund handling. This is partial because configuration decisions and QA remain unresolved.

VALIDATION
Merge, split, and many-to-many scenarios were exercised. A refund example correctly calculated 94 leads at 50 NIS as 4,700 NIS. Final acceptance is blocked on two business decisions.

column1: Account intent pipeline cannot complete its Salesforce write stage
column2:
CONTEXT
An account-based marketing pipeline combines engagement, news, intent, and scoring, then writes a daily Salesforce summary. Collection and scoring modules exist, while scheduling is being prepared separately.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The pipeline needs a destination field, authentication configuration, expanded rendering, and an end-to-end dry run.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each eligible Account should receive a daily rich-text summary. Credentials must use environment variables, live writes must remain switchable, and all required sections must render.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The required Account field does not exist, so writes cannot be tested. The renderer handles only older sections, credentials are not configured, and the scheduler still references an unconfirmed entry-point filename.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The missing Salesforce field is the immediate blocker. Credential names, entry point, dependencies, permissions, and layout also require confirmation.

RESOLUTION
No verified solution has been implemented. Existing modules remain in dry-run mode and no Salesforce writes have been authorized.

VALIDATION
Next steps are to create the destination field, confirm environment-variable names and dependencies, run the complete pipeline in dry-run mode, verify every rendered section across the full filtered account list, and authorize live writes only after review.

column1: Opportunity approval flow creates duplicate review tasks
column2:
CONTEXT
CLIENT_A uses a record-triggered Opportunity flow to create one approval task when Discount_Percent__c exceeds the regional threshold.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Editing an unrelated Opportunity field after submission creates another open approval task for the same record.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Only one open approval task should exist until the current approval cycle is completed.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Every qualifying update creates another task because the flow evaluates only the current discount value.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Flow debug showed that the create-task branch ran on every update. Existing open tasks were not queried, and prior-value conditions were not used. The entry criteria checked only that the discount was above the threshold and did not check that the record had newly entered the approval state.

RESOLUTION
The flow was changed to run when the discount crosses the threshold or the approval status is reset. A Get Records step now prevents creation when an open approval task already exists. Manual task deletion does not automatically reset the Opportunity approval status.

VALIDATION
A new qualifying discount created one task. Five unrelated Opportunity updates created no additional tasks. Resetting and resubmitting the approval created exactly one new task.

column1: Case escalation flow repeatedly updates its own trigger field
column2:
CONTEXT
A Case after-save flow stamps Escalated_At__c and assigns urgent cases to the escalation queue.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Some urgent cases produce repeated flow interviews and eventually fail with a maximum trigger-depth error.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The Case should be reassigned and stamped once.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The flow updates Escalation_Required__c during an after-save execution, causing the same flow to qualify again.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Debug logs showed repeated updates from the same flow interview path. The trigger field remained true after each update. The after-save flow changed a field included in its own entry condition without an idempotency guard.

RESOLUTION
The field updates were moved to a before-save path where possible. The after-save queue assignment now runs only when Escalation_Required__c changes from false to true, and a processed timestamp prevents re-entry. Cases imported with an already populated processed timestamp are intentionally skipped.

VALIDATION
Twenty urgent cases were created and updated. Each produced one assignment and one timestamp, with no recursive interviews or depth errors.

column1: Scheduled renewal actions intermittently remain pending
column2:
CONTEXT
A scheduled flow path sends renewal reminders 30 days before Contract EndDate.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A small subset of contracts reaches the reminder date without producing an email or a failed-flow record.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every eligible active contract should generate one renewal reminder.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Most reminders are sent, but several scheduled actions remain pending beyond their execution time.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The affected records have valid email addresses and meet the flow criteria. Pending-interview exports show the actions, but current logs do not include their execution attempt. The root cause has not yet been identified. Current evidence suggests an execution-capacity or scheduling issue, but this is not verified.

RESOLUTION
No verified resolution is currently available. The issue has been escalated with pending-interview identifiers and execution windows. The frequency is low and the available debug-log retention does not cover all affected executions.

VALIDATION
Not applicable because no corrective change has been implemented.

column1: ERP account retry creates duplicate Salesforce accounts
column2:
CONTEXT
An ERP integration upserts Salesforce Account records using ERP_Customer_ID__c as the external identifier.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Retries after network timeouts occasionally create a second Account for the same ERP customer.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The retry should update or return the existing Account.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
A second Account is inserted when the retry path omits the external-ID field from the upsert request.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Request logs showed that the first path used upsert by ERP_Customer_ID__c, while the retry path used a plain insert. Both payloads contained the same business identifier. The retry handler called a legacy insert method instead of the shared external-ID upsert method.

RESOLUTION
Both initial and retry processing now use the same upsert operation keyed by ERP_Customer_ID__c. The field was also configured as unique. Historical accounts with a missing ERP customer ID require separate cleanup.

VALIDATION
Timeouts were injected before and after commit for 50 payloads. Every retry returned the same Salesforce Account ID and no duplicates were created.

column1: Contact updates are overwritten by older middleware events
column2:
CONTEXT
Contact changes are synchronized bidirectionally between Salesforce and a customer portal through middleware queues.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A newer phone number entered in Salesforce can be replaced minutes later by an older portal event.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The most recent business update should win regardless of delivery order.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Events are applied in arrival order, so a delayed older event overwrites the newer value.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Middleware logs confirmed out-of-order delivery. Payloads include event timestamps, but the Salesforce consumer does not compare them with Last_External_Update__c. The consumer lacks stale-event detection and treats queue arrival time as update order.

RESOLUTION
Timestamp comparison was implemented for phone and email fields. Address fields still use arrival order because the portal currently sends incomplete timestamps. The resolution is partial until reliable timestamps are available for all synchronized fields.

VALIDATION
Out-of-order phone and email events were rejected correctly in 30 tests. Address updates remain under investigation.

column1: Large order batches exceed integration processing window
column2:
CONTEXT
A nightly middleware job sends completed ERP orders to Salesforce in batches of 2,000 records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Peak-day batches exceed the job execution window and leave the final records unsynchronized.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
All orders should complete within the nightly window.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The job times out before processing the last batch segment.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Processing time grows with Salesforce lookup volume. No single record fails; the job reaches its middleware time limit. The current synchronous batch design performs repeated Salesforce lookups and cannot meet the peak-volume window.

RESOLUTION
As a temporary workaround, the job runs in four smaller scheduled waves and resumes from a persisted order cursor. This is not the permanent design. End-to-end completion takes longer, and a queue-based architecture is still required.

VALIDATION
Three peak-size datasets completed without missing orders across four scheduled waves.

column1: Support agents cannot view the customer risk score
column2:
CONTEXT
A calculated Risk_Score__c field is displayed on the Account support layout and used during case prioritization.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Support agents see a blank area where the risk score should appear, while administrators see the value.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Support agents should have read-only visibility of the risk score.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The field is hidden for the Support Agent permission set.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The field contained data and was present on the Lightning page. Field accessibility showed no read permission for the affected permission set. Field-level security was not updated when Risk_Score__c was deployed.

RESOLUTION
Read access to Risk_Score__c was added to the Support Agent permission set while edit access remained disabled. The field remains hidden from external community users by design.

VALIDATION
Three support users could view the score but could not edit it. A user without the permission set still could not view the field.

column1: Regional managers intermittently lose access to transferred accounts
column2:
CONTEXT
Account access is granted through role hierarchy and a criteria-based sharing rule using Region__c.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After ownership transfer, some regional managers can no longer open accounts that still belong to their region.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The manager should retain read access through the regional sharing rule.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Access is retained for most accounts but removed for a subset after transfer.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Affected accounts have the expected Region__c value. Sharing-button output differs between affected and unaffected records, but recalculation timing has not been captured. The root cause is not verified. The current investigation is focused on delayed sharing-rule recalculation and a possible automation change to Region__c.

RESOLUTION
No verified resolution is available. Additional field-history and sharing recalculation logs are required. The issue is intermittent and current logs do not cover the complete ownership-transfer window.

VALIDATION
Not applicable because no corrective change has been implemented.

column1: Integration user cannot create cases after permission-set update
column2:
CONTEXT
A middleware integration creates Case records through a dedicated Salesforce integration user.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
All case-creation requests began failing with insufficient-access errors after a permission-set cleanup.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The integration user should create Cases and populate the approved integration fields.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The API rejects Case creation because Create permission is missing.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Authentication succeeded and field permissions were intact. Permission-set assignment history showed that the legacy set containing Case Create was removed. The replacement integration permission set omitted Case object Create access.

RESOLUTION
Case Create and the required record-type access were added to the scoped integration permission set. The temporary broad permission was removed. New Case fields still require explicit permission review before integration use.

VALIDATION
The integration created test Cases for each supported record type. Attempts to update restricted fields remained blocked.

column1: Revenue dashboard double counts opportunities with multiple products
column2:
CONTEXT
A dashboard reports closed revenue by sales representative using Opportunity and OpportunityLineItem data.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The total revenue exceeds the standard Opportunity report whenever an Opportunity contains multiple products.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each Opportunity amount should contribute once to the revenue total.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Opportunity.Amount is repeated for every line item and summed three times.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The source query joined line items and aggregated the parent Opportunity amount at the child-row level. The dashboard aggregation used a one-to-many line-item dataset without grouping revenue at the Opportunity level first.

RESOLUTION
A separate Opportunity-level aggregate was created for revenue, while product metrics continue to use the line-item dataset. Product-level revenue allocation remains based on line-item totals rather than Opportunity.Amount.

VALIDATION
Totals matched the standard report across Opportunities with zero, one, and multiple products and across two currencies.

column1: SLA report excludes cases closed near midnight
column2:
CONTEXT
A report compares Case ClosedDate with an external SLA calendar grouped by local business date.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Cases closed around midnight appear under the wrong reporting day or disappear from the daily extract.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Cases should be grouped according to the configured business timezone.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The SOQL date literal is evaluated in UTC while downstream grouping assumes local time.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Boundary tests confirmed an offset mismatch. Records outside the boundary are reported correctly. The extraction filter and reporting transformation use different timezone assumptions.

RESOLUTION
The extraction now uses explicit UTC boundaries calculated from the configured timezone. Historical report correction is still pending. The solution is partial until the historical SLA dataset is reprocessed.

VALIDATION
Current-period boundary cases passed for sampled summer and winter dates. Historical aggregates have not yet been rebuilt.

column1: Account activity query exceeds CPU time on large data volume
column2:
CONTEXT
A support dashboard queries recent activities for accounts with several million Task records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The query times out for broad date ranges during peak usage.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The dashboard should return within the interactive timeout.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The filter is not selective enough and the query exceeds the transaction CPU limit.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Query Plan showed a table scan driven by a broad date range and a nonselective custom status filter. The online query design attempts to aggregate a large historical Task population without a selective indexed predicate.

RESOLUTION
As a workaround, the dashboard limits interactive queries to 90 days and uses a nightly summary object for older activity. The workaround introduces nightly latency and does not provide real-time detail beyond 90 days.

VALIDATION
Interactive queries returned within the target for tested high-volume accounts, and summary totals matched sampled historical data.

column1: Customer replies create new cases instead of updating the existing thread
column2:
CONTEXT
Email-to-Case should attach customer replies to the originating Case using Salesforce threading headers.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Replies from one mail gateway intermittently create new Cases.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The reply should be added as an EmailMessage on the existing Case.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The gateway removes the Salesforce reference headers, so Email-to-Case cannot match the reply.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Raw-message comparison showed that the affected gateway stripped In-Reply-To and References headers while another gateway preserved them. Mail-gateway header sanitization removed the identifiers required for reliable case threading.

RESOLUTION
The gateway policy was updated to preserve the required reference headers for the support domain. Subject fallback was disabled. Manually composed messages without reference headers cannot be threaded automatically.

VALIDATION
Replies across three mail clients and both inbound routes attached to the original Case without creating duplicates.

column1: Inbound sales replies are stamped as outbound activities
column2:
CONTEXT
Sales engagement Tasks update the latest activity type on Lead and Contact records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Inbound replies synchronized as Tasks are recorded as Email Sent.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The outbound message should be Email Sent and the reply should be Email Reply.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Both activities are stamped as Email Sent.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Task has no Incoming field equivalent to EmailMessage. The existing flow used a constant outbound value. The Task-based automation hardcoded the activity direction and ignored integration direction metadata.

RESOLUTION
The flow now reads the integration direction marker and applies a newer-activity guard before updating the person record. Legacy Tasks created before direction metadata was introduced remain unclassified.

VALIDATION
Inbound and outbound scenarios passed on both Lead and Contact, including an older delayed Task that was correctly ignored.

column1: Support timeline omits activities older than the archive threshold
column2:
CONTEXT
A custom support timeline displays Account Tasks and EmailMessages for long-term customers.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The component shows no activities older than the platform archive threshold even though users can locate some through standard views.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The timeline should indicate and, where supported, display archived activity.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The custom query returns only current activity and gives no explanation for older records.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Current SOQL and component logic were reviewed. Archived activity behavior differs by API and object, and the intended retention requirement is not yet finalized. No final root cause or supported retrieval design has been confirmed. The current component was built only for non-archived activity.

RESOLUTION
No verified resolution is available. Product and architecture decisions are required before implementation. Platform archive access and performance constraints may prevent a complete real-time timeline.

VALIDATION
Not applicable because no supported solution has been implemented.

column1: Lead conversion creates duplicate contacts for email aliases
column2:
CONTEXT
Lead conversion automation matches existing Contacts by normalized email address.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Addresses containing uppercase characters or plus aliases bypass matching and create duplicate Contacts.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The Lead should match the existing Contact according to the approved alias-normalization policy.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The raw email strings differ and a new Contact is created.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Duplicate-rule logs showed exact email matching. The normalization helper was called during imports but not during interactive conversion. Lead conversion did not apply the canonical lowercase and approved plus-alias normalization used by other ingestion paths.

RESOLUTION
A shared normalized-email field is now populated on both Lead and Contact and used by the conversion matching rule. Alias semantics vary by mail provider, so normalization is limited to approved corporate domains.

VALIDATION
Case, whitespace, and approved alias variants matched correctly; distinct domains and nonapproved aliases remained separate.

column1: Account import matches subsidiaries to the parent company
column2:
CONTEXT
A bulk import uses normalized company name and website domain to match incoming customer Accounts.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Subsidiaries sharing the parent website are merged into the parent Account.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A unique registration number should preserve the subsidiary as a separate Account.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The domain match has higher precedence and selects the parent Account.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Matching logs showed that registration number was evaluated only after domain and normalized name. The match hierarchy prioritizes a shared domain over the stronger legal registration identifier.

RESOLUTION
Registration number now has highest priority when present. The fallback logic for records without registration numbers is still being tuned. The resolution is partial for legacy data lacking registration numbers.

VALIDATION
All reviewed subsidiaries with registration numbers matched correctly. Records without that identifier still produce ambiguous candidates.

column1: Contact owner is not updated after account territory reassignment
column2:
CONTEXT
Business rules require selected Contacts to follow the Account owner when a territory reassignment is completed.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Account ownership changes correctly, but related active Contacts remain owned by the previous representative.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Eligible Contacts should be reassigned to the new Account owner.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The automation queries Contacts before the Account owner update is committed and retains the old owner value.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Flow timing and debug logs confirmed that the Contact update ran in the same before-save transaction using the prior Account owner. The Contact reassignment logic executed before the new Account owner was available.

RESOLUTION
Contact reassignment was moved to an asynchronous after-commit path using the committed Account owner and bulk-safe updates. Contacts with an explicit ownership-lock flag are intentionally excluded.

VALIDATION
Single and bulk territory changes updated all eligible Contacts while excluded Contact types retained their owners.

column1: Pipeline forecast mixes opportunity currencies without conversion
column2:
CONTEXT
A custom forecast aggregates open Opportunity amounts into the corporate currency.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Forecast totals treat EUR and USD amounts as if they were already in the same currency.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each amount should be converted using the configured dated exchange rate.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Raw Opportunity.Amount values are summed without conversion.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The aggregation query selected Amount but not ConvertedAmount, and the transformation assumed corporate currency. The forecast pipeline ignored Salesforce multi-currency conversion fields.

RESOLUTION
The query and aggregation now use converted corporate-currency amounts based on the configured dated rates. Forecast snapshots preserve the rate available at snapshot time and are not retroactively recalculated.

VALIDATION
Forecast totals matched standard Salesforce reports across three currencies and two historical rate periods.

column1: Partial refund report uses original quantity instead of refunded quantity
column2:
CONTEXT
Refund Opportunities track returned units and price per unit for finance reconciliation.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Partial refunds are reported at the full original Opportunity value.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The refund amount should be 1,000 NIS.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The report displays 5,000 NIS because it uses original quantity.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Report formulas referenced Opportunity.Quantity__c instead of Refund_Quantity__c. The refund calculation was mapped to the original sales quantity rather than the quantity actually refunded.

RESOLUTION
The report formula and supporting flow were updated to use Refund_Quantity__c multiplied by Refund_Unit_Price__c. Tax adjustments are handled in a separate finance report.

VALIDATION
Full, partial, and multiple-refund scenarios reconciled with finance examples and did not exceed the original transaction value.

column1: Many-to-many opportunity conversion lacks final allocation rules
column2:
CONTEXT
A conversion process must support merging several original Opportunities into several replacement Opportunities while preserving financial traceability.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The current implementation supports one-to-one and many-to-one conversion but cannot allocate value across many-to-many relationships.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every converted value should be traceable and total allocations should equal the original total.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The UI can create the records but cannot persist a complete allocation matrix.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The existing junction object stores only one source amount per replacement and cannot represent multiple allocations. The current data model does not represent individual source-to-target allocation lines.

RESOLUTION
A junction allocation object has been implemented for one-to-many testing. Many-to-many validation and final UI behavior remain incomplete. The solution remains partial until all allocation paths and reconciliation reports pass QA.

VALIDATION
One-to-many totals and rollback tests passed. Many-to-many scenarios are not yet approved.

column1: Middleware stops synchronizing after Salesforce access token expires
column2:
CONTEXT
A middleware service uses OAuth refresh tokens for continuous Salesforce API access.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Synchronization stops after the access token expires and does not recover automatically.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The service should refresh the token once and retry the failed request.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The refresh succeeds, but the retry still uses the expired token cached in the HTTP client.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Authentication logs showed a new token response followed by a retry carrying the previous Authorization header. The HTTP client cached the original authorization header and was not rebuilt or updated after token refresh.

RESOLUTION
The token provider now updates the shared authorization interceptor atomically before a single controlled retry. A revoked refresh token still requires reauthorization and is escalated explicitly.

VALIDATION
Forced expiry tests across parallel requests recovered successfully and generated only one refresh operation.

column1: Valid payment webhooks fail signature verification after proxy rewrite
column2:
CONTEXT
Payment notifications pass through an API gateway before reaching the Salesforce integration service.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Valid webhooks are rejected because their signatures no longer match the body received by the verifier.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The verifier should validate the exact raw bytes signed by the provider.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The gateway normalizes JSON whitespace before forwarding, changing the signed byte sequence.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Direct requests passed verification. Byte-level comparison showed gateway body transformation before the verifier executed. The proxy rewrites the signed request body, while signature verification requires the original bytes.

RESOLUTION
As a workaround, the gateway forwards a base64 copy of the original body in a protected internal header for verification. The workaround depends on gateway configuration. The preferred long-term solution is a nontransforming webhook route.

VALIDATION
Known valid and tampered payloads were tested; valid signatures passed and modified bodies failed.

column1: Bulk API job remains in UploadComplete without processing
column2:
CONTEXT
A nightly data pipeline uploads Account updates through Salesforce Bulk API 2.0.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
One job remains in UploadComplete for several hours and produces neither results nor failed-record output.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The job should progress to InProgress and then JobComplete or Failed.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The job remains in UploadComplete beyond the normal processing window.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The CSV parses locally, row counts are within previous successful limits, and a smaller subset completes. Platform status and job identifiers have been collected. The root cause has not been identified. Evidence is insufficient to distinguish payload-specific processing from a platform queue issue.

RESOLUTION
No verified resolution is available. The stalled job and payload checksum have been escalated for platform investigation. The split-file approach is diagnostic only and has not been approved as an operational workaround.

VALIDATION
Not applicable because the full workload still cannot complete reliably.

column1: AI query assistant selects service requests for claim questions
column2:
CONTEXT
A Hebrew natural-language assistant generates SOQL over a Salesforce insurance schema.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Questions asking how many claims were opened are routed to the Service Request object.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The query should use the approved Claim object and the current-month CreatedDate filter.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The model selects Service_Request__c and adds an unrelated status condition.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Prompt traces showed overlapping Hebrew synonyms in the schema description, with Service Request listed before Claim. The schema prompt contained ambiguous object descriptions and no explicit routing rule for claim terminology.

RESOLUTION
The schema dictionary was rewritten with explicit domain aliases and a deterministic rule mapping claim terminology to the Claim object. New business synonyms must be added to the maintained schema dictionary.

VALIDATION
A 40-question regression set selected the correct object and avoided unsupported status filters in all claim scenarios.

column1: AI assistant interprets recent customers inconsistently
column2:
CONTEXT
Users ask Hebrew business questions that contain relative terms such as recent, new, and lately.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The assistant translates the same phrase into different date ranges across semantically similar questions.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Ambiguous relative dates should follow a documented default or trigger clarification.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The model alternates between seven, thirty, and ninety days without explaining the choice.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Prompt review found no policy for relative-date expressions. Few-shot examples contain conflicting ranges. The prompt and examples do not define a consistent business meaning for ambiguous date terms.

RESOLUTION
Common sales questions now use documented defaults, while unsupported contexts request clarification. Several specialized intents still lack policies. The solution is partial until all supported intents have explicit temporal policies.

VALIDATION
The main sales regression set passed. Retention and support-domain ambiguity tests still require additional rules.

column1: AI profitability query uses a field from the wrong object
column2:
CONTEXT
The assistant answers questions about the most profitable sales representative by aggregating Lead premium data.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The generated query fails with Invalid field because it selects a Policy-only field from Lead.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The query should aggregate the approved Lead premium field and group by representative ID and name.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The query references Updated_Premium_In_Production__c, which is not defined on Lead.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Schema retrieval returned similarly named Policy and Lead fields without object-qualified examples. The prompt did not enforce object-field compatibility before generating the final SOQL.

RESOLUTION
Object-qualified schema entries and a validation step now reject fields not present on the selected object before execution. The validator checks schema validity but cannot by itself guarantee business-semantic correctness.

VALIDATION
Profitability, claims, and policy regression questions produced valid object-field combinations and correct grouping.

column1: UTF-8 contact import corrupts Hebrew names
column2:
CONTEXT
A migration imports Hebrew Contact names from CSV into Salesforce.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Hebrew characters appear as replacement symbols after import.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
All names should retain their Unicode characters.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The loader reads the UTF-8 file using a legacy Windows encoding.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The source bytes decoded correctly as UTF-8. Loader logs showed the default operating-system encoding was used. The import process did not specify UTF-8 explicitly when opening the CSV.

RESOLUTION
The loader now requires UTF-8, validates decoding before upload, and rejects files containing replacement characters. Files supplied in other encodings must be converted before ingestion.

VALIDATION
Hebrew, Arabic, accented Latin, and plain ASCII samples imported correctly and matched source hashes after normalization.

column1: Legacy customer IDs map to multiple Salesforce accounts
column2:
CONTEXT
A historical migration uses Legacy_Customer_ID__c to connect transactions to Salesforce Accounts.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Several legacy IDs appear on more than one Account after earlier regional migrations.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each active legacy customer ID should identify one canonical Account.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Conflicting regional records prevent deterministic transaction assignment.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Duplicate groups were identified, but some represent true duplicates while others represent valid regional legal entities sharing an old identifier. The root cause is historical identifier reuse across regions; the correct canonical mapping is not yet known for every group.

RESOLUTION
No verified resolution is available for all groups. Ambiguous groups are quarantined for business-owner review rather than automatically merged. Manual business decisions are required before ambiguous historical transactions can be assigned.

VALIDATION
Not applicable to unresolved groups. Unambiguous unique IDs continue to import successfully.

column1: Historical engagement backfill overwrites newer activity
column2:
CONTEXT
A backfill stamps the latest historical email activity onto Lead and Contact records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Running the backfill after go-live can replace a newer live engagement with an older historical record.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The backfill should update a record only when its historical activity is newer than the currently stamped activity.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The backfill updates every matched record without comparing dates.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Execution logs showed unconditional updates. Source ordering was correct, but the target-state comparison was missing. The backfill selected the latest historical source record but did not compare it with the current target engagement date.

RESOLUTION
A date guard now updates only when the source engagement is newer. Equal timestamps are handled idempotently, and dry-run output lists proposed changes. Records with invalid historical timestamps are rejected for manual review.

VALIDATION
Older, equal, newer, null-target, and repeated-run scenarios passed for both Lead and Contact without regression.

column1: Cases remain unassigned when the routing queue lookup returns no records
column2:
CONTEXT
A record-triggered flow assigns new Cases to a support queue based on product line and support tier.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A portion of new Cases stays with the creating user instead of moving to a queue.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every new Case should reach a queue, or the fallback queue when no specific match exists.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Cases created with a product line that has no active routing record keep their original owner and produce no error.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Flow debug logs showed the Get Records element returning no rows for retired product lines. The decision that follows compared the queue variable to specific values, so an empty result fell into the default outcome, which held no assignment action and no fault path.

RESOLUTION
The decision now tests explicitly for an empty queue result and routes those Cases to the general support queue, with a fault path writing failures to a monitoring object.

VALIDATION
Cases created for retired, active, and unknown product lines were all assigned, and the fallback cleared 42 backlog Cases without errors.

column1: Territory realignment flow stops after processing part of the account list
column2:
CONTEXT
A quarterly realignment flow loops through Accounts in a selected region and updates territory and owner fields.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
During the last cycle the flow stopped part way through and left the remaining Accounts unchanged.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A realignment run should process every Account in the selected region in a single execution.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Runs covering more than roughly 1,500 Accounts fail once the interview exceeds the executed-element limit.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The loop performs several decisions and assignments per record, so element consumption grows faster than the record count. Smaller regions complete normally, and the failing runs report a governor limit rather than a data error.

RESOLUTION
Realignment now runs in region chunks of 500 Accounts scheduled 15 minutes apart. This is a temporary mitigation: the loop design is unchanged, and larger regions still require manual splitting. Moving the update logic into a batch Apex job invoked once per region is the preferred long-term solution.

VALIDATION
Three chunked runs completed the largest region without failures, but each cycle still needs manual scheduling and a completion check.

column1: Screen flow clears entered values when users return to a previous screen
column2:
CONTEXT
A guided onboarding screen flow collects customer details across four screens before creating an Account and a Contact.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Agents report that values entered on the second screen are sometimes empty after using the Previous button.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Navigating backward and forward should retain every value already entered in the flow.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Some text and picklist inputs return blank, and agents must retype them before continuing.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Flow variables are assigned on each screen and no clearing assignment exists in the definition. Interview logs from reported sessions show the variables already empty when the second screen is rendered again. The behavior could not be reproduced in the sandbox with the same browser and flow version, and it appears only after an agent spends several minutes on the third screen.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No configuration change has been applied.

VALIDATION
The failure still occurs in production at a low rate. The next step is enabling detailed interview logging for the affected user group and collecting session recordings for a vendor escalation.

column1: Discontinued ERP products remain active and selectable on quotes
column2:
CONTEXT
A nightly middleware job synchronizes the ERP product catalog into Salesforce product records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Products retired in the ERP continue to appear as active and remain selectable on new Quotes.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A retired product should be marked inactive in Salesforce during the next sync cycle.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Retired products keep their active flag, and sales users continue to add them to Quotes.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The ERP clears its lifecycle field when a product is retired instead of sending a retired code. The middleware mapping used a default expression that treated any unrecognized or empty value as active. Payload samples confirmed an empty lifecycle field for every affected product.

RESOLUTION
The mapping now uses an explicit lifecycle table, treats an empty lifecycle value as inactive, and routes unknown codes to an error queue for review instead of defaulting them.

VALIDATION
A replay of the previous week deactivated 168 products, newly retired products were deactivated in the following cycle, and an injected unknown code appeared in the error queue as expected.

column1: New dispute reason codes from the billing platform are rejected on case creation
column2:
CONTEXT
The billing platform sends dispute events that create Cases with a restricted reason picklist.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After the billing platform added two reason codes, a group of dispute events stopped creating Cases.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every dispute event should create a Case, even when its reason code is not yet mapped.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Events carrying the new codes fail with a restricted picklist error and stay in the middleware error queue.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The interface wrote the source code directly into the restricted picklist field, with no fallback value and no alert for unmapped codes. Error queue samples showed only the two new codes failing.

RESOLUTION
A mapping table now translates source codes into approved values, unmapped codes are stored as Other with the raw code kept in a text field, and a daily report lists them for the administrator.

VALIDATION
The 63 queued events replayed successfully, the new codes mapped correctly once added, and an injected unknown code produced a Case marked Other plus a report entry.

column1: Shipment status events arrive before their parent order exists in Salesforce
column2:
CONTEXT
The fulfillment system publishes shipment status events that update Order records through middleware.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Shipment updates for newly created orders are discarded because no matching Order is found.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A shipment event should update its Order regardless of the sequence in which the two systems deliver messages.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Events referencing an order that has not yet synchronized fail the lookup and are dropped without any retry.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The order pipeline and the fulfillment pipeline run on separate schedules, so a shipment can be published minutes before its order record is created. Failed events were not persisted, which made the payloads unrecoverable.

RESOLUTION
Unmatched events are now written to a staging object and replayed every 15 minutes for up to 24 hours. This is a partial solution: the publishing systems still emit events out of sequence, and staged events older than the retention window are discarded after an alert.

VALIDATION
Replay recovered 94 percent of unmatched events over a two-week measurement, and the remainder belonged to orders that never synchronized at all.

column1: Support agents lose access to tasks on cases they own
column2:
CONTEXT
A restriction rule was introduced on the Task object to limit visibility of confidential escalation notes.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After deployment, support agents could no longer see any activities in the related list on their own Cases.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Agents should see Tasks on Cases they own and should be blocked only from notes marked confidential.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The related list shows no activities at all, and logged calls created by the agents themselves are hidden as well.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Restriction rules narrow record access rather than extend it, and the rule criteria matched only Tasks whose type was escalation note. Every other Task therefore fell outside the permitted set. Temporarily deactivating the rule restored full visibility and confirmed it as the cause.

RESOLUTION
The criteria were rewritten to permit Tasks that are not confidential or that are owned by the running user, so confidential notes remain limited to the escalation team.

VALIDATION
Agents saw their own and their team activities, confidential notes stayed hidden from agents, and escalation team members retained full access.

column1: Partner users occasionally see opportunities belonging to another partner account
column2:
CONTEXT
Partner community users access Opportunities for their own partner Account through a sharing set and account-based sharing rules.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Two partner users reported list view rows referencing opportunities from a different partner organization.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A partner user must only see records related to their own partner Account.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Unrelated opportunity rows appear briefly in a list view and are absent after the page is reloaded.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Sharing rules, the sharing set, and the community role hierarchy matched the documented design. Attempts to reproduce the exposure with the same profile, list view, and filters were unsuccessful, and no repeatable sequence was available.

RESOLUTION
No verified root cause or permanent fix exists. The report was treated as a potential security incident: partner access was restricted to minimum required views, affected sessions were revoked, and the security team and platform vendor were engaged. No sharing change was presented as a confirmed fix.

VALIDATION
Targeted tests found no additional cross-account visibility after containment, but the original event remains unreproduced. A recurrence requires immediate capture of record references, session context, and sharing diagnostics.

column1: Field technicians are locked out by login IP restrictions on mobile networks
column2:
CONTEXT
Profile-level login IP ranges restrict access to corporate networks for all internal profiles.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Field technicians working from mobile networks are repeatedly blocked when opening the mobile application.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Technicians should be able to log in from any network while the organization keeps a verified access control.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Logins from carrier networks are rejected because the assigned addresses fall outside the configured ranges.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Login history showed restricted address failures rather than credential failures for the reported users. Carrier address ranges rotate frequently and cannot be maintained as a static allow list.

RESOLUTION
The technician profile no longer defines IP ranges and instead requires multi-factor authentication with device activation, while all other profiles keep their ranges. This is a partial improvement: network-based control is gone for that profile, and a session-level policy with a trusted device requirement remains the intended design.

VALIDATION
Twenty technicians logged in from three carriers over two weeks without restricted address failures, and office profiles still rejected external addresses.

column1: Pipeline extract omits opportunities owned by deactivated users
column2:
CONTEXT
A scheduled SOQL extract feeds the weekly pipeline review with all open Opportunities.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Regional totals in the review were consistently lower than the totals shown in Salesforce reports.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The extract should include every open Opportunity regardless of the owner user status.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Opportunities owned by users deactivated during a reorganization are missing from the extract.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The query filtered on the owner active flag in order to exclude test users created during an earlier project. After the reorganization, 37 genuine opportunities moved to deactivated owners and silently disappeared. Comparing counts against an unfiltered query confirmed the gap and identified the affected owners.

RESOLUTION
The owner status filter was replaced with an explicit exclusion of the internal test user list, and the extract now reports its record count so future gaps are visible.

VALIDATION
The corrected extract matched Salesforce report totals across four regions, recovered the 37 missing opportunities, and still excluded test records.

column1: Case aging metric counts weekends and public holidays as service time
column2:
CONTEXT
An aging metric reports how long open Cases have waited, using the difference between the creation date and the current time.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Support management asked for aging that reflects supported hours instead of elapsed calendar time.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Aging should count only hours inside the configured business hours and exclude holidays.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
A Case created on Friday appears two days older on Monday, which distorts weekly averages and escalation ranking.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The calculation used plain date arithmetic with no reference to the business hours configuration. Holiday records existed but were consumed only by entitlement milestones.

RESOLUTION
The metric now uses the business hours difference for the business hours record assigned to the Case, including its holiday calendar, and stores the result in an aging field refreshed hourly.

VALIDATION
Cases spanning a weekend, a public holiday, and a weekday matched hand-calculated values, and weekly averages fell in line with the removed non-working hours.

column1: Product mix query fails on a cross-object formula filter over full history
column2:
CONTEXT
An analytics job queries opportunity line items filtered by a cross-object formula that resolves the account segment.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The job fails for full-history runs while shorter date ranges complete normally.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The job should return a complete product mix for any requested period.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Full-history runs stop with a query row limit error after several minutes of execution.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Formula fields cannot be indexed, so the filter is applied only after rows are read and the query scans the entire line item table. The query plan confirmed a full table scan with no selective filter available.

RESOLUTION
The job now runs in quarterly ranges using the indexed close date field and merges the partial results. This is a temporary mitigation: the segment filter still evaluates a formula, so runtime grows with data volume. Stamping the account segment onto the line item as an indexed field maintained by automation is the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
Chunked runs completed the full history in 22 minutes and matched report totals, while a single-pass query still fails.

column1: Case replies are sent from a personal address instead of the shared support address
column2:
CONTEXT
Support agents reply to customers from the Case feed, and customers should always see the shared support address.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After a routing change, replies on some Cases were delivered with the individual agent address as the sender.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every Case reply should use the shared support organization-wide address.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Replies on Cases created through the new routing address show the agent address, and customer responses bypass Email-to-Case.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The email action derives its sender from the routing address of the Case origin. The new routing address was created without a link to the shared organization-wide address, so the action fell back to the running user. Cases from the original routing address were unaffected.

RESOLUTION
The new routing address was linked to the shared organization-wide address, and the email action now selects that address explicitly instead of relying on routing configuration.

VALIDATION
Replies from both routing addresses showed the shared sender, and customer responses were threaded back onto the original Case.

column1: Meetings booked through shared team mailboxes are not logged as activities
column2:
CONTEXT
Calendar events from individual mailboxes are captured as Salesforce activities, and account teams also book customer meetings through two shared team mailboxes.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Meetings booked from the shared mailboxes never appear on the Account or Contact timeline.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every customer meeting should appear on the related records regardless of the mailbox that created it.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Only meetings owned by an individual user are captured, and shared mailbox events are ignored because they have no Salesforce user.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The capture configuration maps each mailbox to a licensed user, and shared mailboxes have no such mapping. The events are visible in the calendar service and contain a complete attendee list, so the data is available.

RESOLUTION
A dedicated service user now owns the two shared mailboxes, and captured events are related to Contacts through attendee addresses. This is partial: external attendees without a matching Contact are still not linked, and additional shared mailboxes require manual onboarding.

VALIDATION
Forty shared mailbox meetings were captured and linked correctly over three weeks, while eleven events with only external attendees remained unlinked.

column1: Attachments are missing from some inbound customer emails on the case timeline
column2:
CONTEXT
Inbound customer emails create or update Cases, and their attachments should be stored as files on the Case.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Agents report emails whose body refers to an attached document that is not present on the Case.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every attachment within the accepted size and file type limits should be stored and visible on the Case.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The email record is created normally, but no file is linked and no error appears in the inbound processing logs.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The affected attachments are far below the size limit and use common document types. Retained mail headers for two reported messages show a multipart structure with the attachment part present at delivery. Reprocessing the same stored messages in the sandbox produced the attachment correctly, so the failure is not reproducible from the retained payload.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No configuration or code change has been made.

VALIDATION
The problem continues at roughly one message per week. The next step is retaining full raw inbound payloads for 30 days and comparing a failing message with a successful one from the same sender pattern.

column1: Primary contact roles are lost when duplicate accounts are merged
column2:
CONTEXT
Duplicate Accounts are merged monthly, and open Opportunities move to the surviving Account together with their contact roles.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After recent merges, several open Opportunities had no primary contact role, which blocked quote generation.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Opportunities moved during a merge should keep their contact roles, including the primary designation.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Contact roles that reference Contacts merged in the same operation disappear, and the remaining roles have no primary marked.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Merging a Contact deletes its contact role rows instead of repointing them to the surviving Contact. Comparing pre-merge and post-merge exports for twelve Accounts confirmed that every missing row belonged to a merged Contact.

RESOLUTION
A pre-merge step exports contact roles for both Accounts, and a post-merge job recreates the missing roles against the surviving Contact and restores exactly one primary role per Opportunity.

VALIDATION
Fifteen rehearsal merges in the sandbox preserved every contact role and primary designation, and the following production cycle produced no Opportunity without a primary contact.

column1: Duplicate rule blocks new branch locations that share a billing address
column2:
CONTEXT
A duplicate rule prevents Account creation when the billing address matches an existing Account.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Sales users cannot create branch Accounts for customers whose branches share a registered office address.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Branches with a distinct name or registration number should be allowed, while genuine duplicates remain blocked.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Creation is blocked whenever the billing street and city match, regardless of the account name.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The matching rule relied on exact address matching alone, and name similarity was not part of it. Of 50 blocked attempts reviewed, 31 were valid branches with different names and registration numbers.

RESOLUTION
The matching rule now requires an address match combined with fuzzy name similarity or an identical registration number, and the duplicate rule alerts instead of blocking when only the address matches.

VALIDATION
Replaying the 50 blocked attempts allowed all valid branches, still blocked the 19 genuine duplicates, and produced alerts for address-only matches.

column1: Bulk owner reassignment blanks optional fields on updated cases
column2:
CONTEXT
Support administrators reassign Case ownership in bulk through an export and reload process during team changes.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After the last reassignment, several optional Case fields were empty on the updated records.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A bulk owner update should change only the owner and leave every other field untouched.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Fields that were present but empty in the upload file were cleared on the target records.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The loader configuration still had the insert-null option enabled from an earlier cleanup project, and the exported file contained all fields rather than only the owner. Field history confirmed the values were cleared by the loading user inside the run window.

RESOLUTION
Reassignments now use a two-column template holding only the record key and the new owner, and the insert-null option is disabled before each run. This is a manual control rather than a fix: the loader configuration is shared and can be re-enabled by another administrator. A restricted reassignment tool with a fixed field set is the intended solution.

VALIDATION
Two reassignment runs changed only the owner field, and field history showed no other modifications.

column1: Renewal opportunities are created with prices from an expired price book
column2:
CONTEXT
Renewal Opportunities are generated 90 days before contract end by cloning the original Opportunity and its line items.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Renewal quotes showed unit prices that no longer matched the current price list.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A renewal should use the price book that is active on its close date.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Cloned line items keep their original price book entries, including entries from a price book that expired at the start of the year.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The clone logic copied the price book entry reference directly instead of resolving each product against the active price book. Twenty-eight renewals created after the price change carried outdated prices, with deviations reaching 12 percent on some products.

RESOLUTION
The generator now resolves every product to an entry in the currently active price book, and a validation rule blocks saving line items that reference an inactive entry.

VALIDATION
New renewals used current prices, the 28 affected renewals were reprocessed and matched the published price list, and an attempt to save an inactive entry was rejected.

column1: Revenue splits do not total 100 percent after a sales representative leaves
column2:
CONTEXT
Opportunity revenue splits allocate credit between the owner and supporting representatives for commission reporting.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Commission reports showed unallocated revenue on opportunities that were reassigned after a departure.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Revenue splits on an opportunity should always total 100 percent after any ownership change.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
When a departing representative is removed from the split, the freed percentage is not redistributed and the total stays below 100.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Removing a participant leaves the remaining split rows unchanged, and the offboarding checklist contains no redistribution step. A scan found 46 opportunities with split totals between 40 and 80 percent.

RESOLUTION
A weekly report lists opportunities whose splits do not total 100 percent, and revenue operations corrects them manually. This is a mitigation only: the imbalance is still created at offboarding. Automatic redistribution to the new owner when a split participant is deactivated is the intended fix.

VALIDATION
The report identified all 46 known cases plus three new ones, which were corrected within the same week, but nothing prevents recurrence.

column1: Forecast totals differ between the forecast page and the exported summary
column2:
CONTEXT
Sales managers review a quarterly forecast in Salesforce and also receive an exported summary generated from the same forecast data.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Managers with delegated forecast access report totals in the export that do not match the forecast page.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Both views should present identical category totals for the same manager and period.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Differences of one to four percent appear for some hierarchy managers, and only in the commit and best case categories.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Manager adjustments, currency conversion dates, and the export filter were compared for four managers. Adjustments appear in both views and conversion rates match for the sampled period. The gap did not appear for managers without delegated access, but no direct reproduction was achieved and the affected set changes between refreshes.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. The reconciliation remains open and no change has been applied to either view.

VALIDATION
The differences persist in the current quarter. The next step is a daily snapshot of both totals per manager for a full quarter to determine whether the gap follows adjustment timing or hierarchy changes.

column1: Composite API request rejects an entire batch when one record fails validation
column2:
CONTEXT
A partner portal submits Accounts, Contacts, and Cases together in a single composite API request.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A batch containing one invalid Contact caused the portal to lose every record in that submission.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Valid records in a submission should be saved, and only the invalid ones reported back to the portal.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The whole request is rolled back, and the portal marks all records as failed without retaining the rejected payloads.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The integration sent the composite request with the all-or-none option enabled, so a single validation failure discarded the entire transaction. Stored responses showed one field-level error and a processing-halted response for the remaining subrequests.

RESOLUTION
Dependent records are now grouped into their own composite request with all-or-none enabled, independent records are sent with it disabled, and per-subrequest errors are returned to the portal with the original payload retained for retry.

VALIDATION
A batch with one invalid Contact saved the other 19 records, returned a single field-level error, and the corrected record was retried successfully.

column1: Platform event subscriber stops receiving messages after an extended outage
column2:
CONTEXT
An external service subscribes to a platform event channel and stores the position of the last processed event.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After a maintenance window longer than the event retention period, the subscriber received no further events.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The subscriber should resume from the earliest available event and report the resulting gap.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The subscription is refused because the stored position is older than the retained window, and the client retries the same value indefinitely.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Client logs showed a repeated invalid replay position response that the subscriber did not handle. No alert existed for missing events, so the outage surfaced only when downstream records went stale.

RESOLUTION
The client now detects that response, resubscribes from the earliest retained event, records the gap window, and triggers a reconciliation query for records changed during it.

VALIDATION
A simulated outage beyond the retention window produced automatic resubscription, a gap alert, and a reconciliation that recovered every record changed while disconnected.

column1: Integration clients receive inconsistent field sets across API versions
column2:
CONTEXT
Three external clients read Account and Opportunity data through the REST API, each pinned to a different API version.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
One client reports missing fields that the other clients receive for the same records.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
All clients should retrieve the agreed field set for the objects they consume.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The oldest client receives responses without recently added fields, and describe calls on that version do not list them.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Fields added after an API version was released are not returned by that version. The oldest client runs several releases behind, and no policy required consumers to declare or refresh their version.

RESOLUTION
Two clients were upgraded to the current version and a documented version policy with an annual review was introduced. This is partial: the third client depends on a vendor release scheduled for next quarter and still runs the old version, so its field gap remains open.

VALIDATION
The upgraded clients returned the complete field set in regression tests, while the remaining client still misses four fields, as documented in the policy.

column1: Counting questions return a truncated record list instead of a total
column2:
CONTEXT
An assistant converts business questions into SOQL and returns the results to service managers.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Questions asking how many records exist return a list of records rather than a number.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A counting question should produce an aggregate query and return a single total.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The generated query selects fields with a default row limit, so managers see 200 rows and read that row count as the answer.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The generation prompt applied a fixed row limit to every query as a safety measure, and no intent classification existed. Traces showed the model producing a correct filter but never an aggregate function, while the limit silently capped the result.

RESOLUTION
Questions are now classified as counting, listing, or aggregation before generation. Counting intents produce a count query, the row limit applies only to listing intents, and the response states which intent was used.

VALIDATION
A 60-question regression set produced correct totals for every counting question, matched manually written queries, and preserved the limit for listing questions.

column1: Generated subqueries use object names instead of child relationship names
column2:
CONTEXT
The assistant generates SOQL that includes parent-to-child subqueries, for example related Contacts inside an Account query.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Many generated queries fail to parse whenever they contain a subquery.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Subqueries should use the correct child relationship name for the object pair.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The generated SOQL uses the plural object name, which is invalid for custom objects and for several renamed standard relationships.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The schema description supplied to the model listed objects and fields but not relationship names, so plural forms were inferred. Failures clustered on custom objects, whose relationship names end differently, and on relationships renamed by administrators.

RESOLUTION
A relationship catalog covering the twenty most queried object pairs is injected into the prompt, and generated queries are parsed before execution. This is partial: pairs outside the catalog still rely on inference, and the catalog is refreshed manually.

VALIDATION
Subquery success rose from 54 to 96 percent on a 50-question set, and every remaining failure involved an object pair outside the catalog.

column1: Follow-up questions drop the account filter from the previous query
column2:
CONTEXT
The assistant supports follow-up questions that refine a previous query within the same session.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Some follow-up questions return data for all accounts although the first question was limited to one account.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A refinement should retain the filters of the previous query unless the user removes them explicitly.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The regenerated query occasionally omits the account filter, and the wider result set is presented without any warning.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Session traces show the previous query and its filters present in the context sent to the model, so the filter is dropped during generation rather than lost from the context. The behavior appears mainly from the third turn onward and does not repeat reliably with the same question sequence. Two candidate causes, context truncation and an ambiguous refinement instruction, could not be confirmed.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No prompt or code change has been released.

VALIDATION
The issue still reproduces occasionally in test sessions. The next step is logging the full serialized context for every turn and building a scripted multi-turn evaluation that measures filter retention per turn.

column1: Migrated legacy attachments are created as zero-byte files
column2:
CONTEXT
A migration moves document attachments from a legacy service system into Salesforce files linked to Cases.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A batch of migrated documents opens as empty files although the legacy source holds valid content.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every migrated file should match its source document in size and content.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Roughly nine percent of migrated files have zero size, and the affected records are all larger source documents.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The intermediate export wrote encoded content into a text column with a fixed length, so payloads above that length were truncated and decoded into an empty body. Comparing source and export sizes for a sample showed that every failure exceeded the column limit.

RESOLUTION
The export now streams binary content into individual files instead of a text column, and the loader compares a checksum of each uploaded file with the source before marking the record migrated.

VALIDATION
The 1,240 affected documents were migrated again with matching checksums, and a verification pass across the full set found no remaining zero-byte files.

column1: Migrated cases show the load date instead of the original creation date
column2:
CONTEXT
Historical Cases are migrated from a legacy service desk and must keep their original creation dates for trend reporting.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
All migrated Cases show the migration run date, which makes historical trend reports meaningless.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Migrated Cases should retain the legacy creation date and creating user where a matching user exists.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The creation date equals the load timestamp and the created-by user is the migration account.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The migration mapping supplied audit-field values, but the migration user lacked the permission required to preserve them. The load verification checked only whether records were created, so it did not detect that the supplied creation dates and users were absent from the resulting Cases.

RESOLUTION
The required audit-field permission was assigned, the batch was deleted and reloaded with creation date and creating user, and unmatched legacy users were mapped to a documented placeholder account. Post-load checks were expanded to compare audit fields against the source extract.

VALIDATION
A sample of 200 reloaded Cases matched legacy creation dates and mapped users, monthly volume trends aligned with legacy reports, and the new reconciliation reported no audit-field mismatches.

column1: Account hierarchy import fails when child records load before their parents
column2:
CONTEXT
A migration loads Accounts with a self-lookup that reproduces the legacy parent hierarchy.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Load runs fail for a portion of Accounts with an invalid cross reference on the parent field.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The load should build the full hierarchy in one run regardless of record order.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Records whose parent appears later in the file fail because the parent does not exist yet.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The legacy extract is ordered by account number rather than hierarchy depth, and the loader processes rows in file order. Every failed row referenced a parent positioned further down in the same file.

RESOLUTION
The load now runs in two passes: the first inserts all Accounts without the parent field, and the second updates parent references by external key. This is a workaround: the extract is still unordered and a failed second pass leaves records without parents. A depth-ordered extract from the legacy system remains the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
A rehearsal load of 8,400 Accounts finished without cross-reference errors and matched legacy parent assignments, although the second pass was rerun once after a partial failure.

column1: Community submissions fail with an unhandled fault on a hidden required field
column2:
CONTEXT
A screen flow lets authenticated community users submit service requests that create Case records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Submissions from community users end with a generic unhandled fault screen and no Case is created.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The flow should create the Case or present a clear message describing what the user must correct.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Internal users complete the same flow successfully, while community submissions fail at the create step.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Fault screen details showed a validation rule requiring an internal routing code. That code is populated by a separate internal automation that does not run for community profiles, so the field was always empty at create time. The flow had no fault path, so the platform message reached the user directly.

RESOLUTION
The flow now sets a default routing code for community submissions, and the validation rule was scoped to exclude records created through the community entry point. A fault path returns a readable message.

VALIDATION
Twenty community submissions across three request types created Cases with the correct routing code, and a deliberately invalid submission returned the readable message instead of a fault screen.

column1: Scheduled path actions run on records that no longer meet the entry criteria
column2:
CONTEXT
A record-triggered flow uses a scheduled path to send a follow-up reminder five days after a Case is marked pending customer.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Customers received reminders for Cases that had already been resolved or reopened by an agent.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A scheduled action should run only if the record still satisfies the condition that queued it.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Reminders are sent based on the state captured when the path was scheduled, regardless of later status changes.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Scheduled paths evaluate entry criteria when the interview is queued, not when it executes. Pending interview exports showed queued actions for Cases whose status had changed within the waiting period, and the path contained no re-evaluation step.

RESOLUTION
The scheduled path now begins with a Get Records step that reloads the Case and a decision that ends the interview when the status is no longer pending customer.

VALIDATION
Cases resolved during the waiting window produced no reminder, Cases still pending received exactly one, and a status change and revert still produced a single reminder.

column1: Records created by platform event automation are owned by the automated process user
column2:
CONTEXT
A platform event triggered flow creates follow-up Tasks when the fulfillment system reports a delivery exception.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The created Tasks do not appear in any agent work list and are invisible in team reports.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each Task should be owned by the account owner or by the exception handling queue.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Every Task is owned by the automated process user, so ownership filters in list views and reports exclude them.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
