Platform event triggered flows run as the automated process user, and the create element did not assign an owner. Because the field was left empty it defaulted to the running context user rather than to a business owner.

RESOLUTION
The flow now resolves the related Account owner and assigns it explicitly, falling back to the exception handling queue when the owner is inactive.

VALIDATION
Fifty simulated exception events produced Tasks owned by the correct representative, inactive owners routed to the queue, and team reports showed the full volume.

column1: Two record-triggered flows on Account overwrite each other's field values
column2:
CONTEXT
Two before-save record-triggered flows on Account maintain a segment field and a service tier field.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The segment value is sometimes correct after a save and sometimes reverts to its previous value.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Both automations should apply their calculations to the same record without discarding each other's results.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Whichever flow runs second writes a segment value derived from data it read before the first flow updated it.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Both flows were built without a trigger order value, so their execution sequence is not guaranteed. Debug logs from consecutive saves showed the two flows running in a different order, which matched the alternating results. The second flow recalculated segment from a stale in-memory value.

RESOLUTION
The segment logic was consolidated into a single before-save flow, and the remaining flow was given an explicit trigger order so future automations cannot interleave.

VALIDATION
Two hundred sequential and bulk Account updates produced a stable segment value, and debug logs confirmed a deterministic execution order.

column1: Approval notifications are silently dropped when the assigned approver is inactive
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow sends an in-app notification and an email to the approver named on a discount request.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Some discount requests waited for days with no approver acknowledgement and no error report.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every request should notify an active approver, or escalate when the named approver is unavailable.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Requests whose approver has left the company are created normally, but no notification is delivered.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Send actions targeting an inactive user complete without a delivery, and the flow treated the action as successful. A report of pending requests showed that all stalled records referenced deactivated users, none of which had been removed from the approver matrix.

RESOLUTION
The flow now checks the approver active flag, escalates to the approver's manager when the user is inactive, and logs the substitution on the request record.

VALIDATION
Requests routed to an inactive approver escalated to the manager within a minute, active approvers were unaffected, and the pending backlog cleared after reprocessing.

column1: Recalled approval requests leave records locked for editing
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow locks Quote records when an approval request is submitted and unlocks them when the request is approved or rejected.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Users who recall their own approval request can no longer edit the Quote they recalled.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Recalling a request should return the Quote to an editable state for the submitter.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The record stays locked, and only an administrator can unlock it manually.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The unlock logic ran on approval and rejection outcomes only. Approval history for the affected Quotes showed a recall event with no matching unlock action, and the lock flag remained set on every one of them.

RESOLUTION
The flow now handles the recall outcome and unlocks the record, and a scheduled job reports Quotes that stay locked for more than one day without an open approval request.

VALIDATION
Recalled Quotes became editable immediately, approved and rejected paths were unchanged, and the scheduled report returned no stale locks over two weeks.

column1: Bulk enrichment load triggers a mass update far wider than intended
column2:
CONTEXT
A record-triggered flow copies enrichment values from an industry code onto related Contacts.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
An enrichment load touched 40,000 Accounts and rewrote Contact fields that the load never supplied.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The automation should update Contacts only when the industry code actually changes.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Any Account save re-applies the mapped values, so a load that rewrote unrelated fields propagated defaults to every related Contact.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The entry condition tested that the industry code was not empty rather than that it had changed. Field history showed Contact updates with identical before and after values on most records and genuine overwrites on approximately 1,900.

RESOLUTION
The entry condition now uses a prior-value comparison, and the update skips Contacts whose values already match. This is partial: the 1,900 overwritten Contacts still need a source-based restore, and only three of eight fields have a reliable external source.

VALIDATION
A rehearsal load of 5,000 Accounts produced no Contact updates, and targeted code changes updated only affected Contacts. Historical restoration is incomplete.

column1: Flow fault emails flood administrators after every large data load
column2:
CONTEXT
Several record-triggered flows send the default fault email to the flow owner when an element fails.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Large data loads generate thousands of fault emails, and genuine failures are lost among them.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Failures should be recorded in a reviewable form with a single summary notification per load.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Each failed record produces an individual email, and administrator mailboxes reach delivery limits during a load.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Fault paths were absent, so the platform default email applied. Sampling 300 messages showed that most originated from one flow failing on records locked by an active approval process, which is an expected condition rather than a defect.

RESOLUTION
Fault paths now write structured entries to an error log object, and a scheduled job sends one digest per hour. This is partial: the underlying flow still attempts updates on locked records, so the log grows during loads and the condition is suppressed rather than avoided.

VALIDATION
A 20,000 record load produced two digest emails and 640 log entries instead of individual messages, and a genuine configuration error was visible in the digest.

column1: Paused flow interviews resume an hour late after the daylight saving change
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow pauses until a fixed local time each morning before sending a daily dispatch summary to field teams.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After the seasonal clock change, the summary arrived an hour later than the agreed dispatch time.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The summary should always arrive at the agreed local time regardless of seasonal offsets.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The resume time is calculated from a stored offset, so interviews paused before the change resume against the previous offset.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The wait configuration used a datetime built from a static offset value rather than a timezone-aware calculation. Interviews created after the change resumed correctly, which confirmed that only the stored pending interviews were affected.

RESOLUTION
The stored offset is adjusted manually twice a year, and pending interviews are recreated after the change. This is a workaround: the calculation is still offset based, and a missed manual step reproduces the problem. Rebuilding the wait on a timezone-aware schedule is the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
After the manual adjustment the summary arrived on time for three weeks, but the correction depends on an operator remembering it.

column1: Record-triggered flow does not fire for a subset of integration-created cases
column2:
CONTEXT
A record-triggered flow stamps a priority score on every Case at creation, including Cases created by middleware.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Roughly two percent of integration-created Cases have no priority score and never entered the automation.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every created Case should produce a flow interview and receive a score.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Affected Cases exist with complete field data, but no interview, error, or fault entry is recorded for them.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The affected records match the entry criteria when re-saved manually, and the score is applied correctly on that second save. The gap is not tied to one middleware batch, one record type, or one time of day. Debug logs for the integration user were enabled for three days but no failing creation was captured in that period.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No change has been deployed.

VALIDATION
Affected Cases continue to appear at a low rate. The next step is continuous debug logging for the integration user with correlation identifiers written by the middleware so a failing creation can be traced end to end.

column1: Invoice totals drift by small amounts after middleware rounds currency values
column2:
CONTEXT
Middleware transfers invoice header and line amounts from the billing platform into Salesforce records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Finance reported invoice totals in Salesforce that differ from the billing platform by a few cents.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Amounts in Salesforce should match the source system exactly for every invoice and line.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Line amounts match, but headers differ on invoices with many lines, and the difference grows with line count.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The transformation converted amounts through a floating point type with two-decimal rounding on each line, then summed the rounded values. The source computes the header from unrounded line values. Recalculating twenty sample invoices reproduced the difference exactly.

RESOLUTION
The mapping now carries decimal values without intermediate rounding, and the header amount is taken from the source rather than recomputed downstream.

VALIDATION
A replay of 4,000 invoices matched the source to the cent, including the twenty previously failing samples, and a reconciliation report showed no remaining variance.

column1: Curated legal account names are overwritten by the ERP nightly feed
column2:
CONTEXT
Account records receive a nightly update from the ERP, while the data stewardship team maintains verified legal names in Salesforce.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Corrected legal names revert to abbreviated ERP spellings within a day of being fixed.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Fields owned by the stewardship team should not be modified by the integration.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The nightly feed writes every mapped field, including the curated name, whenever the ERP record has any change.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The mapping had no concept of field ownership and updated all mapped fields on every payload. Field history confirmed the integration user as the last modifier on all reverted records, always within the nightly window.

RESOLUTION
A field ownership matrix was defined, the curated fields were removed from the write mapping, and the ERP value is now stored in a separate reference field so differences remain visible.

VALIDATION
Curated names survived ten nightly cycles, the reference field continued to receive ERP values, and stewardship reports could compare both.

column1: Contacts deleted in the ERP remain active in Salesforce
column2:
CONTEXT
The ERP is the source of record for employee contacts at customer organizations, and middleware keeps Salesforce aligned.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Contacts removed in the ERP stay active in Salesforce and continue to receive campaign messages.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A contact removed at the source should be deactivated in Salesforce during the next cycle.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Only creates and updates arrive, so removed records remain untouched with no indication that they are obsolete.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The ERP export contains active rows only, and the middleware treats an absent row as no change. Comparing a full export with Salesforce found 812 contacts present only in Salesforce, most removed more than a year earlier.

RESOLUTION
The ERP now emits a deactivation flag on removal, and a weekly full comparison marks contacts missing from the source as inactive with a reason code instead of deleting them.

VALIDATION
The 812 obsolete contacts were deactivated and excluded from campaigns, a test removal propagated within one cycle, and no active contact was deactivated in error.

column1: A single malformed message blocks the entire account integration queue
column2:
CONTEXT
Account changes flow through an ordered middleware queue that preserves sequence per record.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Account updates stopped reaching Salesforce for several hours while the source system continued publishing.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A message that cannot be processed should be set aside so the remaining traffic continues.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
One message with an unparsable date field was retried continuously at the head of the queue and blocked every message behind it.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The consumer retried indefinitely on any exception and had no attempt ceiling. Queue metrics showed a single message with several thousand attempts and a backlog that grew steadily behind it.

RESOLUTION
The consumer now retries three times with increasing intervals, moves failed messages to a dead letter queue with the original payload, and raises an alert when that queue is not empty.

VALIDATION
An injected malformed message moved to the dead letter queue after three attempts, the backlog drained within four minutes, and the alert fired once.

column1: Appointment times from the scheduling system are stored an hour off for half the branches
column2:
CONTEXT
A scheduling system publishes customer appointments that middleware writes into a Salesforce datetime field.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Branch staff report appointments displayed one hour earlier than booked, but only at some locations.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
An appointment should display at its booked local time for every branch.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Branches in one region show the correct time while branches in another show a one hour shift that changes with the season.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The source publishes wall clock time with a separate location field, and the middleware appended a fixed offset for all records. Comparing bookings across the seasonal change confirmed the shift followed daylight saving rather than the booking itself.

RESOLUTION
The middleware now resolves each branch to its timezone identifier and converts wall clock time using that zone before writing the datetime value.

VALIDATION
Two hundred bookings across six branches and both seasonal periods matched the source, and previously affected appointments were corrected by a targeted replay.

column1: Bidirectional account sync echoes its own updates back into Salesforce
column2:
CONTEXT
Account data synchronizes in both directions between Salesforce and the ERP through middleware.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A single user edit produces several update cycles between the two systems and inflates integration volume.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
An update should propagate once and then stop.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The ERP acknowledgement is written back to Salesforce, which raises a new outbound event, and the loop repeats until the values are identical.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
No marker distinguished integration-originated updates from user updates. Message traces showed three to five cycles per edit, and volume peaks matched the enrichment batch window rather than user activity.

RESOLUTION
Outbound events now carry an update source marker that the middleware suppresses on the return path. This is partial: bulk jobs on the ERP side submit changes without the marker, so batch-originated echoes still occur and are limited only by a value comparison.

VALIDATION
Interactive edits now propagate exactly once across 300 sampled changes, while the monthly ERP batch still produced one redundant cycle per record.

column1: Leads with free-text country values are rejected by the marketing platform sync
column2:
CONTEXT
Qualified Leads are exported to a marketing platform that requires a two-letter country code.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A recurring share of Leads fails export and never enters a nurture campaign.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every qualified Lead should reach the marketing platform with a valid country code.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Leads whose country field contains a spelled-out or misspelled country name are rejected by the target schema.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The Salesforce country field is free text on the web form, and the export passed it through unchanged. Analysis of 3,000 rejected Leads found 47 distinct spellings covering 18 countries, including local-language names.

RESOLUTION
A normalization table covering those 47 variants was added to the export, and unmatched values are reported daily. This is partial: the source field remains free text, so new variants will keep appearing until the web form uses a restricted picklist.

VALIDATION
Rejections fell from about 6 percent to 0.4 percent over three weeks, and the remaining failures were new spellings captured by the daily report.

column1: Nightly full-load synchronization no longer fits the maintenance window
column2:
CONTEXT
A nightly job reloads the complete customer master from the source system into Salesforce.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The job now runs into business hours and competes with user activity.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Synchronization should complete inside the maintenance window as data volume grows.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Runtime has grown with record count because every record is sent whether or not it changed.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The source cannot emit change events, and its modification timestamp is unreliable for records updated by batch processes. A comparison run showed that fewer than four percent of records change on a typical night.

RESOLUTION
The job now sends a delta based on a content hash calculated during extraction, with a full reload once per month. This is a workaround: hash comparison still requires reading the full source, and deletions are detected only during the monthly reload. Source-side change capture remains the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
Nightly runtime fell from five hours to 40 minutes with matching record counts after each run, while the monthly full reload still takes the original window.

column1: Integration updates leave no trace of the business user who made the change
column2:
CONTEXT
Middleware writes updates from a partner portal into Salesforce using a single integration user.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Support cannot tell which portal user requested a change when investigating disputed data.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each record change should be attributable to the person who initiated it.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Field history shows only the integration user, and the portal audit trail is not linked to Salesforce records.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Salesforce attributes changes to the authenticated API user, and the portal identity is present in the payload but was never mapped. Sampled disputes required manual cross-referencing of portal logs by timestamp, which took hours per case.

RESOLUTION
The payload identity is now stamped into a source-user text field and a change reason field on each write. This is a workaround: field history still names the integration user, and the stamped value can be overwritten by a later update. Per-user authenticated access remains the preferred design.

VALIDATION
Thirty sampled changes carried the correct portal identity, and dispute investigation time dropped from hours to minutes.

column1: Concurrent integration streams intermittently fail with record lock errors
column2:
CONTEXT
Two middleware streams write to Salesforce in parallel, one updating Accounts and one updating related Contacts.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A small share of updates fails with a record lock error and requires manual replay.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Parallel streams should complete without contention, or retry transparently.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Failures appear in short bursts, and the same payload succeeds when replayed minutes later.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Failures cluster on Accounts with many child Contacts, which is consistent with parent locking during child updates, but the streams were traced for a week without a reproducible overlap. Timestamps of failing calls do not consistently overlap between the two streams, so a third writer cannot be excluded. Batch sizes and ordering were reviewed and match the documented configuration.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No change has been made to either stream.

VALIDATION
Failures continue at roughly 0.3 percent of calls. The next step is enabling correlated request logging on both streams and rerunning a controlled test that writes to the same parent from both sides at a known interval.

column1: Nested public group membership grants unintended access to executive report folders
column2:
CONTEXT
Report folder access is granted to public groups, and one group includes another group to simplify administration.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A team lead discovered that regional analysts could open executive compensation reports.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Executive report folders should be visible only to the executive reporting group.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Analysts inherited folder access because their group was nested inside a group that had been added to the executive folder.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Access was removed from the affected group immediately and the folder was restricted while the review continued. Group membership was expanded programmatically and showed 46 users receiving access through two levels of nesting. Folder sharing had been granted to the parent group during an earlier reorganization.

RESOLUTION
The nested group was removed from the folder, executive folders now use a dedicated group with direct membership, and a monthly review report lists effective folder membership after expansion.

VALIDATION
Expanded membership dropped from 46 users to 9, analysts confirmed the folder is no longer visible, and the review report matched the approved list.

column1: Muted permissions in a permission set group block access that individual sets grant
column2:
CONTEXT
Support roles receive access through a permission set group that combines several permission sets with a muting set.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After a group update, agents lost the ability to edit the knowledge article status field.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Agents should retain every permission granted by the component sets except those intentionally muted.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The field is read-only for all agents even though one component set grants edit access.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The muting set had been extended with a broad object-level mute that also covered the field. Comparing effective permissions before and after the change showed the mute applied to two fields beyond the intended one, since muting overrides all grants in the group.

RESOLUTION
The muting set now targets only the intended field, and a deployment check compares effective permissions for a sample user before and after any group change.

VALIDATION
Agents regained edit access on the status field, the intentionally muted field stayed read-only, and the comparison check flagged a deliberate test regression.

column1: Field history tracking was lost on a compliance field during a deployment
column2:
CONTEXT
A consent field on Contact must be history tracked to satisfy an internal audit control.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
An audit sample found no history entries for consent changes made over the previous two months.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every consent change should produce a field history entry retained for the required period.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Consent values changed on many records, but the history related list is empty for that period.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The object metadata deployed two months earlier did not include the history tracking attribute, so the setting was replaced during deployment. Setup audit trail confirmed the deployment date, which matches the first missing entry. History for the period cannot be reconstructed.

RESOLUTION
History tracking was re-enabled, the deployment source now includes the attribute, and a post-deployment check verifies tracked fields against a control list. The audit gap was documented and reported to the compliance owner.

VALIDATION
New consent changes produce history entries, the control check detected a deliberately removed attribute in a sandbox deployment, and the compliance owner accepted the documented gap.

column1: A guest sharing rule exposed contact records through a public form lookup
column2:
CONTEXT
A public web form on the community site uses a lookup to associate a request with an existing organization.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A tester found that the lookup returned Contact names and job titles to unauthenticated visitors.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Guest users should search Accounts only and should never receive Contact data.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The lookup returned Contact records because a sharing rule granted the guest user read access to a Contact set.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The site was taken offline and the sharing rule was removed immediately as containment. A legacy sharing rule created for an earlier campaign granted read access to Contacts owned by a marketing queue. Event monitoring for the exposure window showed lookup queries but no evidence of bulk retrieval, and the security team was notified.

RESOLUTION
The sharing rule was deleted, the lookup was restricted to Accounts with a filtered search layout, and guest access is now reviewed against a documented baseline each release.

VALIDATION
The lookup returned no Contact data in retesting, a permission report showed no remaining guest access to Contact, and the baseline review is scheduled.

column1: An Apex controller running without sharing returns records the user cannot open
column2:
CONTEXT
A Lightning component lists related service agreements through an Apex controller.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Users saw agreement summaries in the component that they could not open from the record page.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The component should display only records the running user is permitted to see.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The list includes agreements owned by other regions, and clicking one produces an insufficient access error.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The controller class was declared without sharing, so its query ignored sharing rules while the detail page enforced them. Testing with three regional users reproduced the mismatch consistently, and the exposed fields included contract value.

RESOLUTION
The class now runs with sharing, the query enforces field-level security through user mode access, and a test class asserts that a restricted user receives no cross-region rows.

VALIDATION
Regional users saw only their own agreements, the new test failed against the previous class version, and the security review signed off the change.

column1: Multi-factor exemption remains in place for a shared automation profile
column2:
CONTEXT
Multi-factor authentication is required for all interactive logins, with an exemption for automation accounts.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A security review found the exemption assigned to a profile that also serves interactive administrators.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Only dedicated API-only accounts should hold the exemption.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Four users share the exempt profile, and two of them log in through the user interface.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Login history confirmed interactive sessions on the exempt profile. Two integrations authenticate with that profile and cannot present a second factor, so the exemption could not simply be removed.

RESOLUTION
The two interactive users were moved to a standard profile with multi-factor enforced, and the exempt profile is now API-only with an IP allowlist. This is partial: one scheduled legacy job still authenticates with a shared credential on that profile, and its migration to a service integration depends on a vendor upgrade.

VALIDATION
Interactive logins on the exempt profile stopped, the allowlist rejected an out-of-range test login, and the legacy job remains a documented exception.

column1: Encrypted identification numbers cannot be used in compliance reports
column2:
CONTEXT
A national identification field on Contact was encrypted at the platform level to satisfy a data protection requirement.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The compliance team can no longer group or filter their monthly report by that field.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Compliance reporting should continue while the underlying value stays protected.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Encrypted fields are not available for filtering, grouping, or sorting, so the existing report returns unusable output.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The limitation is inherent to the encryption method rather than a configuration error. The report needed only the issuing country and a validity flag, not the full number, which suggested a derived value would be sufficient.

RESOLUTION
Two derived fields hold the issuing country and a validity flag, populated when the number is written, and the report uses those. This is a workaround: the derived values duplicate part of the protected data and must be maintained by automation. A reporting model that queries the source in a protected context is preferred.

VALIDATION
The monthly report reproduced its previous totals for three periods, and the identification number remained unreadable in reports and list views.

column1: Territory-based sharing grants wider access than the regional data policy allows
column2:
CONTEXT
Account access is granted through a territory model that mirrors the sales hierarchy.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A data protection review found that representatives in one region can open customer records from a restricted region.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Access must stop at the regional boundary defined in the data policy.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Territory grants follow the reporting hierarchy, which spans regions above the country level.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The hierarchy was built for forecasting rather than data residency, and several managers hold roles above two regions. An access review found 23 users with cross-region visibility, all through legitimate hierarchy grants rather than misconfiguration.

RESOLUTION
Restricted-region Accounts were moved to a dedicated territory branch with hierarchy access disabled. This is a workaround: forecasting roll-ups for that branch must now be assembled manually, and the underlying model still couples access to the sales hierarchy. A redesign separating the two remains outstanding.

VALIDATION
The 23 users no longer see restricted records, spot checks confirmed correct access for in-region users, and forecast roll-ups required manual assembly for one cycle.

column1: Field access is intermittently lost for a subset of users after a package upgrade
column2:
CONTEXT
A managed package supplies custom fields on Opportunity that sales operations users edit daily.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After the last package upgrade, some users intermittently find those fields read-only for part of a day.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Field access should remain stable for all users holding the package permission set.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Affected users report read-only fields, and access returns later without any administrative action.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Permission set assignments were verified as unchanged during the affected periods, and a permission report for two affected users showed edit access at the time of review. No profile or field-level security change appears in the setup audit trail for those days. The affected users are spread across three profiles, and no shared automation or login pattern has been identified.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No permission change has been applied, since the current evidence does not identify what to change.

VALIDATION
Reports continue at two to three per week. The next step is a scripted hourly capture of effective field permissions for the affected users, together with a support case referencing the package version and upgrade date.

column1: Unusual bulk export activity detected on a shared reporting service account
column2:
CONTEXT
A shared service account is used by an internal reporting tool to extract data on a fixed schedule.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Monitoring flagged export volume from that account at several times its normal level outside the scheduled window.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The account should extract only its scheduled datasets during defined hours.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Large exports ran at irregular times, and the reporting tool owner cannot account for all of them.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The credential was rotated, the account was restricted to the reporting server address range, and the security team opened an incident as immediate containment. Login history shows connections from outside the reporting infrastructure. The credential was also shared with a decommissioned analytics tool, so the origin cannot yet be attributed.

RESOLUTION
No verified root cause exists. Containment is in place, but the source of the exports is unidentified and no conclusion about intent or impact has been reached.

VALIDATION
No further out-of-window exports have been observed since the restriction. The next step is a forensic review of event monitoring data and a search for other systems holding the retired credential.

column1: Grouped service report silently drops cases with an empty category
column2:
CONTEXT
A monthly service report groups Cases by a category picklist to show volume per support area.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The report total is consistently lower than the case count shown on the support dashboard.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every closed Case in the period should appear in the report under a category or an explicit unspecified group.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Cases with an empty category are absent from the grouped output and from the report total.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The underlying query groups by the category field and the extraction filtered out empty values to avoid a blank row label. A count comparison found 1,430 Cases in the period with no category, most created through the email channel where the field is not required.

RESOLUTION
The extraction now maps empty categories to an unspecified bucket rather than excluding them, and the email channel sets a default category at creation.

VALIDATION
Report totals matched the dashboard for three prior months, the unspecified bucket showed the expected volume, and new email Cases carried the default category.

column1: Unique customer metric counts the same account once per transaction
column2:
CONTEXT
A quarterly metric reports how many distinct customers made a purchase, calculated from an aggregate query over Orders.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The reported customer count exceeds the total number of active accounts in the region.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The metric should count each customer once regardless of how many orders they placed.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Customers with repeat orders are counted once per order, so the figure grows with order volume rather than reach.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The query used a plain count over the order rows rather than a distinct count of the account reference. Recalculating one quarter with a distinct count produced a figure 38 percent lower and consistent with the account base.

RESOLUTION
The metric now uses a distinct count of the account reference, and the order count is published separately so both figures remain available.

VALIDATION
Four historical quarters were recalculated and stayed below the active account total, and a manual check of one region matched the new figure exactly.

column1: Activity report filters on record creation instead of the activity date
column2:
CONTEXT
A weekly report shows completed customer activities per representative for the selected week.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Representatives report that activities they logged for earlier visits appear in the wrong week.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
An activity should be counted in the week in which it took place.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Activities logged several days after the visit are counted in the week they were entered.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The query filtered on the record creation timestamp instead of the activity date field. A sample of 500 activities showed 22 percent were logged at least one day after the visit, with the largest gaps after multi-day field trips.

RESOLUTION
The report now filters and groups on the activity date, and a secondary column shows the entry delay so late logging remains visible to managers.

VALIDATION
Recalculated weeks matched manually reconciled visit logs for four representatives, and the delay column identified the field trip pattern.

column1: Exported dashboard component stops at the row limit without any warning
column2:
CONTEXT
A dashboard component lists open opportunities by owner and is exported weekly for a management review.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The exported file consistently ends part way through the alphabet with no error message.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The export should contain every row behind the component or state clearly that it was limited.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The file stops at a fixed number of rows, and readers assume the remaining owners have no pipeline.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The component inherits a row limit applied to detail exports, and the truncation is silent. Comparing the export against a direct query showed 2,000 exported rows against 3,417 actual rows, with the missing rows sorted after the cut-off.

RESOLUTION
The review now uses a summarized export grouped by owner, which returns one row per owner, and a scheduled extract supplies the full detail file when needed.

VALIDATION
The summarized export listed all 214 owners with totals matching the direct query, and the detail extract returned all 3,417 rows.

column1: Margin percentage is blank whenever a cost value is missing
column2:
CONTEXT
A margin percentage formula divides the difference between revenue and cost by revenue on each opportunity line.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Product profitability reports show blank margins for a group of lines and an understated average.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Lines without a cost value should be identified rather than silently excluded from the average.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Any line with an empty cost produces an empty margin, and the report average is calculated over the remaining lines only.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Empty numeric fields propagate through the formula, so the result is empty rather than zero. Of 12,000 lines, 900 had no cost, all from a supplier feed that stopped sending cost values after a schema change.

RESOLUTION
The formula now treats an empty cost as unknown and sets a data quality flag, the report excludes flagged lines from the average and lists them separately, and the supplier feed mapping was corrected.

VALIDATION
The flagged count fell to zero for new records, historical flagged lines were listed in a review tab, and the average margin changed by 3.2 points once complete data was included.

column1: Attainment percentage compares quarterly results with monthly targets
column2:
CONTEXT
An attainment metric divides achieved revenue by the sales target stored on a target object.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Attainment figures appear roughly three times higher than the sales operations team expects.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Achieved revenue for a period should be compared with the target covering the same period.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Quarterly revenue is divided by a single monthly target row, so results are inflated for every representative.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Targets are stored per representative per month, and the join selected the first matching row instead of aggregating the three months in the quarter. Recomputing one quarter with summed targets produced figures consistent with the operations plan.

RESOLUTION
The metric now aggregates target rows across the selected period before dividing, and it reports a warning when any month in the period has no target row.

VALIDATION
Recalculated attainment matched the operations plan for two quarters and 40 representatives, and the missing-target warning correctly identified three new hires.

column1: Historical trend breaks after support categories were renamed
column2:
CONTEXT
A trend report tracks case volume per support category across three years.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Categories renamed during a service redesign appear as new series that start mid-year while older series end abruptly.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A renamed category should present one continuous series across the full period.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Historical records keep the previous label because the rename did not rewrite stored values, so each rename splits the trend.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Comparing the picklist definition with stored values found 14 labels no longer in the active set. Eleven map cleanly to a current category, while three were split into two categories each, so their history cannot be attributed without reclassification.

RESOLUTION
A mapping table now aligns the 11 unambiguous labels to current categories. This is partial: the three split categories remain grouped under a legacy bucket, and resolving them requires manual reclassification of about 4,000 Cases.

VALIDATION
Eleven series are continuous across three years and match manual counts for two sampled quarters, while the legacy bucket still holds the unresolved volume.

column1: Executive dashboard shows figures that lag the underlying data by hours
column2:
CONTEXT
An executive dashboard aggregates several large reports and is opened throughout the day.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Executives see numbers that do not match the operational reports they open minutes later.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Dashboard figures should reflect data no older than the stated refresh interval.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Refreshes are queued behind other scheduled jobs, so components can display values from several hours earlier without indicating their age.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Refresh history showed queued runs during the daily peak. The source reports each scan large volumes, and their combined runtime exceeds the interval between scheduled refreshes.

RESOLUTION
A summary object is now populated hourly by a batch job, and the dashboard reads that object while displaying the snapshot time. This is a workaround: figures are still not live, and the summary must be extended whenever a new breakdown is requested. Moving the dashboard to an analytics platform remains the preferred direction.

VALIDATION
Dashboard components rendered in under three seconds with a visible snapshot time, and hourly values matched the operational reports at the same timestamp.

column1: Archive queries cannot filter on the fields the audit team needs
column2:
CONTEXT
Closed interactions older than three years are archived into a big object to keep the transactional model small.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The audit team cannot retrieve archived interactions by product or resolution code.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Auditors should be able to filter archived interactions by the same attributes they use on live data.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Queries filtering on product or resolution code are rejected because those fields are not part of the archive index.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
A big object can only be filtered on its defined index fields, and the index was built on account and date at design time. Changing the index requires rebuilding the object and reloading roughly 60 million rows.

RESOLUTION
A nightly extract copies archived rows into an external warehouse where auditors query freely. This is a workaround: the warehouse copy duplicates archived data and lags by a day, and the archive index is unchanged. Rebuilding the object with a richer index remains the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
Auditors completed two review cycles against the warehouse copy, and row counts matched the archive for every sampled month.

column1: Nightly extract returns a different row count on each run of the same period
column2:
CONTEXT
A nightly job extracts closed opportunities for a fixed prior period into a reporting store.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Re-running the job for the same period returns counts that differ by a few dozen rows.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A query over a closed historical period should return identical results on every run.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Counts vary between runs, and the differing records are not the same set each time.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The period is fully in the past and the affected records show no modification during the runs. The job pages through results with a query locator, and the variance appears only on runs crossing more than twelve pages. The query specifies no sort order, which makes page boundaries unstable; adding an explicit sort still produced a small variance in two test runs.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. The explicit sort change was not promoted, since it did not eliminate the variance.

VALIDATION
The variance persists at roughly 0.1 percent of rows. The next step is capturing the identifiers returned on each page across repeated runs and comparing boundary records to establish whether rows are skipped.

column1: Order confirmation template leaves related product details blank
column2:
CONTEXT
An order confirmation template merges customer details and the primary product name into a message sent from the Order record.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Customers receive confirmations in which the product section is empty.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every confirmation should include the primary product name and delivery window.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Customer fields merge correctly while the product fields render as empty text.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The template referenced fields on the order line object, which is a child collection rather than a single related record, so no value could be resolved. Confirmations for orders with one line were equally blank, which ruled out a data issue.

RESOLUTION
Two formula fields on Order now expose the primary product name and delivery window, and the template merges those fields instead of traversing to the child object.

VALIDATION
Confirmations for single-line and multi-line orders rendered the product section correctly, and a test order with no lines produced a documented placeholder rather than an empty section.

column1: Automated replies between two mailboxes generate an endless case thread
column2:
CONTEXT
Inbound support mail creates Cases and sends an automatic acknowledgement to the sender.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
One Case accumulated several hundred messages overnight and consumed a large share of the daily email allocation.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Automated messages should be recorded without triggering another automated reply.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The acknowledgement reached an automated mailbox at the customer that replied automatically, and both systems continued responding to each other.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The message headers on every loop message carried an auto-submitted marker, which the acknowledgement rule ignored. Message timestamps showed a reply every few seconds, and the loop stopped only when the daily limit was reached.

RESOLUTION
The acknowledgement rule now skips messages carrying auto-response headers, and a guard suppresses further replies after three automated messages on the same thread within an hour.

VALIDATION
A simulated auto-responder exchange produced one acknowledgement and stopped, normal customer replies were unaffected, and the guard logged the suppressed attempt.

column1: Customer notifications are filtered as spam after the sending domain change
column2:
CONTEXT
Transactional notifications are sent from Salesforce using a corporate sending domain.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Delivery complaints rose sharply after the company adopted a new sending domain.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Notifications should reach the inbox with authenticated sender records aligned to the visible sender address.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Messages arrive in junk folders or are rejected outright by several recipient providers.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Message headers showed authentication passing for the technical envelope sender but not aligning with the visible sender domain, which several providers treat as a failure. The new domain was published with sender policy records but without matching signing keys for the platform.

RESOLUTION
Signing keys were generated for the new domain and published, the visible sender address now uses that domain, and a delivery monitoring report tracks authentication results by provider.

VALIDATION
Header checks on test messages showed aligned authentication for four major providers, junk placement stopped in seed testing, and the complaint rate returned to the previous baseline within a week.

column1: Engagement tracking is missing for recipients who receive plain text messages
column2:
CONTEXT
Outbound campaign messages record open and click engagement on the related Contact.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A group of Contacts shows no engagement at all despite replying to the same campaigns.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Engagement should be recorded for every recipient where tracking is technically possible.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Contacts marked to receive plain text messages have no open or click records, and reports treat them as unengaged.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Open tracking relies on an embedded image that plain text messages cannot carry, so the absence is expected rather than a defect. Of 6,800 Contacts, 540 carried the plain text preference, and their reply rate was comparable to tracked recipients.

RESOLUTION
Reports now exclude plain text recipients from engagement rate denominators and show them as a separate untracked segment, while click tracking was enabled through tagged links where the preference allows it.

VALIDATION
Engagement rates rose to expected levels once the untracked segment was separated, and the segment count matched the preference field exactly.

column1: All-day meetings occupy the wrong span on the customer timeline
column2:
CONTEXT
Customer meetings appear on the account timeline with their start time and duration.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
All-day workshops appear as short late-evening entries instead of full-day items.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
An all-day event should render across the whole day it covers.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The timeline shows a one-minute entry at the end of the day for every all-day event.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
All-day events store a date without a time component, and the timeline component treated the missing time as midnight before applying a timezone conversion that shifted it backwards. Ordinary timed events rendered correctly, which isolated the all-day flag as the differentiator.

RESOLUTION
The component now checks the all-day flag and renders those events as full-day items without timezone conversion.

VALIDATION
All-day, multi-day, and timed events rendered correctly for users in three timezones, and existing events required no data change.

column1: Automated notifications are not visible on the case they relate to
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow sends status notifications to customers when a Case moves to a waiting state.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Agents cannot see those notifications on the Case and sometimes repeat the same message manually.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every automated customer message should appear in the Case activity history.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Customers receive the messages, but the Case shows no corresponding email record.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The send action addressed a recipient email string and set only the related Contact, so no Case association was stored. Comparing sent-message logs with Case activity confirmed the messages were delivered but never linked.

RESOLUTION
The send action now sets the Case as the related record and the Contact as recipient, which stores the message in the Case activity history.

VALIDATION
Notifications appeared on the Case within seconds for 60 test transitions, historical messages were reconciled from the send log, and duplicate manual messages stopped being reported.

column1: Hard bounced addresses continue to receive automated messages
column2:
CONTEXT
Bounce events from the email service are recorded against Contacts and Leads.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Addresses that hard bounced weeks ago still receive automated messages, which harms sender reputation.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A hard bounced address should be suppressed until it is corrected and revalidated.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The bounce is recorded on the record, but sending processes do not consult it before dispatch.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Only the marketing platform honoured the bounce flag. Automated flows and agent quick actions send through a different path with no suppression check. A review of one month found 1,700 messages sent to previously bounced addresses, 90 percent from automated flows.

RESOLUTION
A shared suppression check now runs in every automated send path and blocks flagged addresses with a logged reason. This is partial: agent-initiated messages still bypass the check, since the send action does not support it, and those cases rely on a warning banner on the record.

VALIDATION
Automated sends to bounced addresses dropped to zero over two weeks, while the banner reduced but did not eliminate agent sends.

column1: Campaign sends exceed the daily message allocation during peak weeks
column2:
CONTEXT
Product update campaigns and transactional notifications share the same daily message allocation.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
During campaign weeks, transactional notifications fail late in the day because the allocation is exhausted.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Transactional messages must always be delivered, and campaign traffic should adapt to the remaining capacity.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Campaigns consume the allocation early, and order confirmations sent afterwards fail silently.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Sends were dispatched in the order requested with no classification. Daily counters showed campaigns consuming most of the allocation before midday on peak days, with transactional failures concentrated in the afternoon.

RESOLUTION
Messages are now classified, transactional traffic holds a reserved share, and campaign batches are metered against the remaining capacity. This is partial: on the busiest days campaign messages still spill into the following day, and the allocation itself has not been increased.

VALIDATION
No transactional failure occurred across two campaign weeks, while campaign completion was delayed by a day on three occasions.

column1: Mail sent to a legacy support alias reaches the wrong triage queue
column2:
CONTEXT
Regional support queues each have their own routing address, and a legacy company-wide alias still forwards into the same system.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Customers writing to the legacy alias land in the default queue regardless of their region.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A message should reach the queue that serves the customer's region.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Forwarded messages carry the alias as the destination, so region-based routing has nothing to match on.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Routing keys on the destination address, which is identical for every forwarded message. The original recipient survives in a forwarding header that the routing rules do not read. About 18 percent of inbound volume still arrives through the alias.

RESOLUTION
A triage rule now assigns queue by the sender's account region when the destination is the alias. This is a workaround: senders with no matching account still land in the default queue, and correct routing depends on account data quality. Retiring the alias after a customer communication campaign is the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
Region assignment was correct for 82 percent of alias traffic in a two-week sample, with the remainder from unmatched senders.

column1: Message opens are recorded within seconds of sending for some recipients
column2:
CONTEXT
Open events are recorded per recipient and feed an engagement score used for lead prioritization.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Sales users distrust the score because some contacts show an open one or two seconds after the send.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
An open should reflect a person viewing the message rather than an automated process.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Immediate opens appear for recipients at certain organizations, often followed by no further engagement.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Affected recipients cluster by email domain rather than by campaign or template, which is consistent with protective scanning at the recipient side, but that cannot be confirmed from the data available. Requests recorded for those opens carry generic client information. Two contacts confirmed they had not opened the messages attributed to them.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or correction exists. Nothing has been changed in the scoring model, since the origin of the events is not established.

VALIDATION
The pattern persists across recent campaigns. The next step is a controlled send to a seed list on the affected domains with distinct tracking assets, to compare recorded events with known recipient behavior.

column1: Record type picklist values disappear after a metadata deployment
column2:
CONTEXT
Case record types restrict the reason picklist to values relevant for each service line.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After a release, agents working the technical record type could select only two reason values instead of eleven.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each record type should offer its full configured value set after any deployment.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Nine values are missing from the technical record type while remaining available on others.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The deployment package included the picklist field but not the record type value assignments, so the target values were reset to the packaged subset. Comparing the record type metadata between sandbox and production confirmed the missing assignments and the deployment timestamp.

RESOLUTION
The value assignments were restored, the deployment package now includes record type metadata, and a post-deployment check compares available values per record type against a control list.

VALIDATION
All eleven values returned for the technical record type, other record types were unchanged, and the check flagged a deliberately incomplete test package.

column1: Leads created through the API bypass the active assignment rules
column2:
CONTEXT
Assignment rules distribute incoming Leads to regional sales queues.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Leads created by the web integration remain with the integration user and are never worked.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every new Lead should be assigned by the active assignment rule regardless of its creation channel.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Leads created through the user interface are assigned correctly, while API-created Leads keep the creating user as owner.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Assignment rules run for API inserts only when the request asks for them explicitly, and the integration did not set that option. A count of unassigned Leads matched the integration volume for the same period, and no rule entry criteria excluded them.

RESOLUTION
The integration now sets the assignment rule header on insert, and a scheduled report lists Leads still owned by the integration user after ten minutes.

VALIDATION
Two hundred test Leads routed to the expected queues, the backlog was reassigned by a one-time job, and the scheduled report has returned no rows since.

column1: Gaps in contract numbering are treated as missing records during audit
column2:
CONTEXT
Contracts carry an auto-generated number used as the reference in customer correspondence.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
An internal audit questioned gaps in the number sequence and asked where the missing contracts were.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The numbering scheme used for audit purposes should be gapless or documented as non-sequential.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Numbers skip values after failed saves and deletions, which auditors read as evidence of removed records.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Auto-number fields consume a value per attempt, so gaps are expected behavior rather than data loss. Reconciling three sampled gaps against record history showed two failed validations and one deleted draft, all accounted for.

RESOLUTION
The auto-number remains as a technical key, and a separate gapless audit reference is now assigned by automation only when a contract is activated. The numbering behavior was documented for the audit team.

VALIDATION
The audit reference ran without gaps across 1,200 activations including deliberate failed saves, and the audit team accepted the documented explanation.

column1: Activities stay on the previous account after a contact is reparented
column2:
CONTEXT
Contacts move between Accounts when a person changes employer within a customer group.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
After a move, the new Account shows no interaction history for that person.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Activities that belong to the person should follow them to the new Account.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Tasks and events keep the previous Account reference, so the history stays with the former employer.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Activities store the Account reference captured at creation and do not follow later Contact changes. A review of 60 reparented Contacts found every historical activity still linked to the previous Account, including activities logged the same week as the move.

RESOLUTION
A flow now updates related activities to the new Account when a Contact is reparented, excluding activities explicitly linked to an opportunity or a case that stays with the original Account.

VALIDATION
Fifteen sandbox reparenting scenarios moved the expected activities and left linked opportunity activities in place, and the production backlog was corrected by a one-time job.

column1: Validation rules block the enrichment job from completing its updates
column2:
CONTEXT
A nightly enrichment job updates firmographic fields on Accounts from a data provider.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The job reports thousands of failures each night and leaves records partially enriched.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Enrichment should complete for every record, while user-entered data keeps its validation requirements.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Updates fail on Accounts missing a manually maintained field that a validation rule requires on any save.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Three validation rules apply to every update regardless of context. Error samples showed the same three rule names across 94 percent of failures, all on legacy Accounts created before the rules existed.

RESOLUTION
A custom permission identifies the enrichment user, the three rules now exclude that permission, and a data quality report lists legacy Accounts still missing the manual field so they can be corrected by their owners.

VALIDATION
The nightly job completed with zero validation failures for two weeks, interactive saves still enforced the rules, and the data quality report listed 640 legacy Accounts for follow-up.

column1: Address standardization covers domestic records but leaves international formats inconsistent
column2:
CONTEXT
A standardization service normalizes billing addresses so that reporting and shipping use consistent formats.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Regional reports still show the same city written in several ways, which splits totals.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Addresses should be normalized to one consistent format regardless of country.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Domestic addresses are normalized reliably, while international addresses are returned unchanged or partially parsed.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The service subscription covers domestic reference data only, and international lookups return a low confidence result that the integration accepted as-is. Of 22,000 Accounts, 5,400 are international, and 3,100 of those had inconsistent city spellings.

RESOLUTION
Low confidence results are now rejected rather than written, and a curated alias table normalizes the 40 most frequent international cities. This is partial: the remaining international addresses stay unnormalized until the reference data subscription is extended.

VALIDATION
Domestic consistency stayed at 99 percent, the 40 curated cities merged into single report rows, and 1,900 international addresses remain unnormalized and flagged.

column1: Web form submissions create duplicate leads before matching completes
column2:
CONTEXT
Website enquiries create Leads that a matching service later links to existing customers.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Visitors who submit the form twice within a short period create two Lead records.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A repeat submission from the same person should update the existing Lead rather than create another.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The matching service runs after insert, so both submissions are created before either is evaluated.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The web endpoint inserts first and matches asynchronously to keep the form responsive. Submission logs showed 340 duplicate pairs in a month, most within four minutes of each other, typically after a visitor corrected a typo and resubmitted.

RESOLUTION
A scheduled job merges duplicate pairs every 15 minutes and notifies the owner. This is a workaround: duplicates still exist between runs and can both be picked up by sales, and the underlying insert-then-match order is unchanged. Synchronous matching at the endpoint is the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
The job merged 340 historical pairs and now clears new duplicates within one cycle, though two cases of parallel outreach were reported during the window.

column1: Long customer notes are truncated when copied into the summary field
column2:
CONTEXT
An automation copies the latest customer note into a summary field used in list views and reports.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Agents found summaries cut off mid-sentence, and some appeared to change meaning.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The summary should present readable content and make clear when the full note is longer.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The copy is truncated at the target field length without any indication that content follows.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The source note allows 32,000 characters while the summary field allows 255. The automation assigned the value directly, so the platform truncated it. A sample showed 28 percent of notes exceeded the limit, with an average length of 640 characters.

RESOLUTION
The automation now truncates at a word boundary and appends a marker showing the note continues. This is a workaround: the summary still cannot hold the full note, and reporting on note content remains incomplete. Reporting directly against the note object is the preferred approach.

VALIDATION
Sampled summaries ended at word boundaries with the marker present, and agents confirmed the meaning was no longer distorted in 30 reviewed records.

column1: A small number of cases lose their contact relationship overnight
column2:
CONTEXT
Cases carry a Contact reference used for correspondence and entitlement checks.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Agents find Cases each morning where the Contact field is empty although correspondence exists on the record.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The Contact reference should persist for the life of the Case unless an agent changes it.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Between five and fifteen Cases per night lose the reference, and the field history shows the change without a recognizable actor.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Field history attributes the change to the integration user, but the nightly integration payloads reviewed for three dates contain no Contact field. The affected Cases share no record type, queue, or account. Disabling one suspected job for two nights did not stop the occurrences.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No automation has been permanently disabled, since the responsible process has not been identified.

VALIDATION
The nightly losses continue. The next step is enabling fine-grained logging for the integration user during the overnight window and adding a trigger-level capture that records the call context whenever the field is cleared.

column1: Active records are found in the recycle bin without a matching deletion entry
column2:
CONTEXT
Deletion of customer records is restricted to administrators and should always appear in the audit trail.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Forty active Accounts were found in the recycle bin with no entry in the deletion review report.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every deletion should be traceable to an authorized user or process.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The records were deleted within a two-hour window, and no available log identifies the actor.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The records were restored and the delete permission was suspended for all non-administrator profiles as immediate containment, and the security team was informed. The records share an owner who was on leave and whose session history shows no activity in that window. A data loading tool used by two teams is a candidate, but its logs had already passed their seven-day retention.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause exists. Containment is in place, but the deletion source is unidentified and no conclusion has been drawn about intent.

VALIDATION
No further unexplained deletions have occurred since the permission change. The next step is extending tool-side log retention, enabling delete event monitoring, and replaying a controlled deletion to identify the actor.

column1: Opportunity amount stops matching its line items after a product swap
column2:
CONTEXT
The opportunity amount is normally derived from the sum of its product lines and drives pipeline reporting.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Deals where a product was replaced show an amount that no longer matches the line total.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The amount should always equal the sum of the current lines unless it is deliberately overridden.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Replacing a product leaves the amount at its earlier value, and the difference persists into the forecast.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
An earlier automation wrote the amount directly during a bulk correction, which converted the field to a manually maintained value on those records. Comparing 200 mismatched deals showed all had been touched by that correction, while untouched deals recalculated normally.

RESOLUTION
The affected records were reset so the amount is derived from lines again, the bulk correction script was retired, and a daily report lists deals whose amount deviates from the line total.

VALIDATION
Product swaps on 40 test deals recalculated correctly, the 200 historical records matched their line totals after the reset, and the daily report has returned no new deviations.

column1: Quarterly bookings exclude deals closed in the last week of the fiscal period
column2:
CONTEXT
The company uses a custom fiscal calendar in which quarters end on a Saturday rather than a month boundary.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Bookings reported for the quarter are lower than the figures sales leadership tracks manually.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Bookings should include every deal closed within the fiscal quarter as defined by the custom calendar.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Deals closed between the fiscal quarter end and the calendar month end are pushed into the next period.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The reporting extract used calendar month boundaries while the organization runs a custom fiscal calendar. Reconciling two quarters showed 63 deals landing in the wrong period, all closed in the overlap days at each quarter boundary.

RESOLUTION
The extract now reads fiscal period boundaries from the calendar definition instead of deriving them from calendar months, and the reporting layer groups by fiscal period.

VALIDATION
Two recalculated quarters matched leadership figures exactly, the 63 misplaced deals moved to their correct period, and a boundary test with a deal closed on the final Saturday landed correctly.

column1: Annual recurring revenue is inflated by placeholder subscription lines
column2:
CONTEXT
Recurring revenue is calculated from active subscription lines on renewal contracts.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Reported recurring revenue exceeds the amount that finance recognizes by a growing margin.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The calculation should include only lines that represent billable recurring commitments.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Placeholder lines created with zero quantity for future options are included at their list price.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The calculation multiplied unit price by term without checking quantity, so zero-quantity lines contributed their full list value. Sales teams create these placeholders during negotiations, and 1,150 active contracts carried at least one.

RESOLUTION
The calculation now requires a positive quantity and an active status, and placeholder lines are marked with a dedicated line type that reporting excludes.

VALIDATION
Recalculated recurring revenue came within 0.3 percent of the finance figure across three months, and a test contract with placeholders contributed only its billable lines.

column1: Terminated contracts still generate automatic renewal opportunities
column2:
CONTEXT
A scheduled process creates renewal opportunities for contracts approaching their end date.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Account managers received renewal tasks for customers who had already terminated their agreements.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Renewals should be created only for contracts that are active and not marked for termination.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Contracts with a termination notice keep their original end date, so they still match the date-based selection.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The selection filtered on end date and an active flag that is cleared only when the term actually expires, not when notice is received. Fourteen renewal opportunities were traced to contracts with a recorded termination notice, two of which reached the customer.

RESOLUTION
The selection now excludes contracts with a termination notice or a non-renewal flag, and the two customer-facing errors were withdrawn with an apology by the account team.

VALIDATION
A rerun over the previous quarter produced no renewals for terminated contracts, valid renewals were unchanged, and a test termination removed the contract from the next selection.

column1: Commission tiers are applied to gross revenue instead of net revenue
column2:
CONTEXT
Commission is calculated on net revenue after discounts and returns, using tiered rates per representative.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Several representatives were paid at a higher tier than their actual performance justified.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Tier thresholds should be evaluated against net revenue as defined in the compensation plan.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The calculation compares gross revenue with the thresholds, then applies the resulting rate to net revenue.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The tier lookup and the payout base used different fields, which only becomes visible for representatives near a threshold. Recalculating one quarter showed 9 of 74 representatives crossing a tier boundary they had not reached on net revenue.

RESOLUTION
The tier lookup now uses net revenue, the calculation logs both figures for transparency, and the nine affected payouts were corrected with finance through the standard adjustment process.

VALIDATION
A full quarter recalculation matched the compensation plan for all 74 representatives, and boundary test cases produced the expected tier on both sides of each threshold.

column1: Usage-based billing data is complete for only part of the product portfolio
column2:
CONTEXT
Usage-based products are billed from consumption data collected by the platform team and loaded into Salesforce.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Revenue operations cannot produce a complete usage forecast because some products have no consumption data.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every usage-based product should report consumption on the same schedule and granularity.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Two products report daily consumption, while three others provide only a monthly total supplied manually.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Only the two newer products emit metering events. The remaining three run on an older platform whose export is a manual spreadsheet, and its totals are not broken down by customer contract.

RESOLUTION
Daily consumption for the two instrumented products now loads automatically with contract-level attribution, and forecasting uses it directly. This is partial: the three legacy products remain manual and monthly, so the forecast for them is an estimate until the platform team adds metering.

VALIDATION
Automated products reconciled with the billing system for two months within 0.5 percent, while legacy products were reconciled only at the monthly total level.

column1: Revenue schedules are not adjusted when a subscription is upgraded mid-term
column2:
CONTEXT
Multi-year subscriptions generate monthly revenue schedule rows used for recognition reporting.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Upgrades taken in the middle of a term are not reflected in the remaining schedule rows.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Remaining periods should be regenerated at the new value from the upgrade effective date.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Schedule rows keep the original amount, so recognized revenue understates the contract from the upgrade date onward.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Schedules are generated once at contract activation and never revisited. A review found 87 upgrades in the last two quarters, all with unchanged schedules, and the difference reached 18 percent on the largest contract.

RESOLUTION
An upgrade now regenerates future schedule rows from the effective date while leaving closed periods untouched. This is partial: downgrades and mid-term cancellations still require a manual correction, since their proration rules are not yet agreed with finance.

VALIDATION
Twenty test upgrades regenerated the correct rows and left closed periods intact, and the 87 historical contracts were corrected in a controlled batch.

column1: Credit memos recorded as negative opportunities distort pipeline reporting
column2:
CONTEXT
Customer credits are recorded so that net revenue reporting reflects them alongside sales.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Pipeline and win rate metrics are skewed because credits appear as opportunities with negative amounts.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Credits should reduce recognized revenue without appearing in pipeline or conversion metrics.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Negative opportunities are counted as deals, which lowers average deal size and inflates the closed count.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
No dedicated object existed for credits, so the team reused the opportunity model. A review found 430 negative opportunities in a year, all created by two finance users and all closed on the day they were created.

RESOLUTION
Credits are now marked with a dedicated record type that every pipeline report excludes, while revenue reports still include them. This is a workaround: credits remain opportunities, so any new report must remember the exclusion. A separate credit object linked to the original deal is the preferred design.

VALIDATION
Pipeline metrics recalculated without credits matched the finance view of bookings, and average deal size rose to the expected range across four quarters.

column1: Consolidated invoices cannot be attributed back to individual opportunities
column2:
CONTEXT
Invoices from the billing platform are matched to opportunities so that closed revenue can be verified.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
