A group of invoices remains unmatched every month and blocks the revenue reconciliation report.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each invoice should be attributable to one or more opportunities with a documented allocation.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Consolidated invoices covering several agreements arrive as a single line with no reference to the underlying deals.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The billing platform consolidates at the customer level for around 12 percent of accounts, and the payload carries no deal identifier. Matching by amount was tested and failed because consolidated totals include proration and credits. The billing team confirmed that deal-level references are not stored at invoicing time.

RESOLUTION
No verified approach exists. Amount-based matching was rejected during testing, and no allocation rule has been agreed with finance.

VALIDATION
Roughly 300 invoices per month remain unmatched. The next step is a joint session with the billing team to determine whether a deal reference can be carried through consolidation, and to define an allocation rule if it cannot.

column1: Stage duration metrics show negative values for some opportunities
column2:
CONTEXT
A sales velocity report measures how long opportunities spend in each stage using stage history records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A small number of opportunities report negative durations, which breaks the average for their segment.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Stage duration should always be zero or positive and should sum to the total age of the opportunity.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Some opportunities have history rows whose timestamps are out of sequence, producing negative intervals.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The affected opportunities were all updated by both a user and an automated process within the same second, and their history rows carry identical timestamps in a non-chronological order. Ordering by the record key instead of the timestamp produced plausible durations in a test, but the key order could not be shown to reflect the true sequence. Roughly 200 of 45,000 opportunities are affected.

RESOLUTION
No verified fix exists. The alternative ordering was not adopted, since its correctness is unproven.

VALIDATION
Negative durations still occur on new records at a similar rate. The next step is instrumenting the automation to write an explicit sequence stamp on stage change so ordering no longer depends on history timestamps.

column1: External application inserts fail after a field became required
column2:
CONTEXT
A partner application creates service requests through the REST API using a documented field set.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
All inserts from the partner application began failing shortly after an internal release.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A schema change should either remain compatible with published integrations or be coordinated with them.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Every insert is rejected because a newly required field is absent from the partner payload.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
A release added a required custom field to support internal reporting, with no default value and no exclusion for API contexts. Error responses named the field consistently, and the failure start time matched the deployment.

RESOLUTION
The field now carries a default value and is required through a validation rule scoped to interactive users only, and the release checklist includes a review of published integration contracts.

VALIDATION
Partner inserts resumed immediately with the queued backlog accepted, interactive users are still required to complete the field, and the checklist caught a similar change in the following release.

column1: Reporting client processes only the first page of query results
column2:
CONTEXT
An external reporting client queries Opportunities through the REST API and loads the results into a data store.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The reporting store consistently holds fewer records than Salesforce for the same filter.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The client should retrieve every record matching the query.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Exactly 2,000 records arrive per run regardless of how many records match.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The API returns results in pages with a continuation reference when more remain, and the client read the first response only. The response body showed the completeness flag set to false and a continuation reference that was never followed.

RESOLUTION
The client now follows the continuation reference until the response is marked complete, and it compares the returned total with the record count before declaring a run successful.

VALIDATION
A run over 21,400 matching records retrieved all of them, the count check failed deliberately when a page was skipped in a test, and daily loads have matched Salesforce totals since.

column1: Nightly integration window exceeds the concurrent long-running request limit
column2:
CONTEXT
Several integrations run concurrently at night, each issuing large queries against Salesforce.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Some integrations receive a concurrency error and abort mid-run several nights a week.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Scheduled integrations should complete without competing for the same platform allocation.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
When more than ten long-running requests overlap, additional requests are rejected until earlier ones finish.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Four integrations were scheduled at the same start time, and each opened multiple parallel connections. Request logs showed peaks of 14 concurrent long-running calls, and every failure occurred during those peaks rather than on any specific query.

RESOLUTION
Queries were narrowed with selective filters so most complete below the long-running threshold, connection counts were capped per integration, and start times were staggered across the window.

VALIDATION
Peak concurrency dropped to six over two weeks with no concurrency errors, and total window duration decreased by 25 minutes.

column1: Bulk upsert fails when the same external key appears twice in one job
column2:
CONTEXT
A daily bulk job upserts customer master records using an external identifier as the match key.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Entire batches fail with duplicate key errors even though the target records are unique in Salesforce.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The job should upsert each distinct external key once per run.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Batches containing the same external key twice are rejected, because a single job cannot upsert the same key more than once.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The source extract emitted one row per source-system address, so customers with two addresses produced two rows sharing the same key. Failed batches always contained at least one such pair, and about 4 percent of records were affected.

RESOLUTION
The extract now consolidates addresses into a single row per external key, and a pre-load check rejects a file containing duplicate keys before the job starts.

VALIDATION
Three full loads completed with no duplicate key errors, a deliberately duplicated file was rejected by the pre-load check, and address data remained complete after consolidation.

column1: Outbound callouts lose a required header after a named credential change
column2:
CONTEXT
Apex callouts to a logistics provider authenticate through a named credential and send a required tenant routing header.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
All callouts began returning an authorization error after the credential was migrated to the newer configuration format.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Callouts should carry both the authentication header and the routing header after the migration.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Requests are authenticated but rejected by the provider, whose response indicates a missing routing header.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Custom headers defined on the previous credential were not carried into the new external credential structure. A request trace confirmed the header was absent while the authorization header was present. No secret value was exposed during the trace, and the provider's error message named the missing header explicitly.

RESOLUTION
The routing header was redefined on the new external credential, and a smoke test that asserts every required header now runs after any credential change.

VALIDATION
Callouts succeeded immediately after the change, the smoke test failed as expected when a header was removed in a sandbox, and the provider confirmed normal traffic.

column1: Outbound rate limiting protects the REST endpoint but not the legacy interface
column2:
CONTEXT
Salesforce sends order updates to a supplier through a modern REST endpoint and an older interface used for corrections.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The supplier reported that bursts of traffic overwhelmed their systems during a large campaign.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Outbound traffic should stay within the agreed request rate across all interfaces.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
REST traffic respects the agreed rate, while corrections sent over the legacy interface arrive in unthrottled bursts.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Rate limiting was implemented in the shared REST client, which the legacy path does not use. Traffic captures during the campaign showed the REST path holding steady at the agreed rate while the legacy path peaked at four times that level.

RESOLUTION
The REST limiter was extended with a shared counter so both paths draw from one budget for reporting. This is partial: the legacy path can read the counter but cannot yet queue requests, so it slows only when the shared budget is already exhausted.

VALIDATION
Combined traffic stayed within the agreed rate on two of three campaign days, with one burst recorded when corrections were submitted before REST traffic began.

column1: Provider cannot deliver callbacks, so status updates depend on polling
column2:
CONTEXT
A payment provider publishes transaction status changes that must be reflected on Salesforce records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Status changes appear in Salesforce long after the provider records them.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A status change should be reflected within a few minutes of occurring at the provider.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Provider callbacks cannot reach the middleware, because inbound connections from that network are blocked by policy.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The security policy prohibits inbound connections from the provider network, and a review confirmed no approved path exists. The provider offers a change feed that can be polled, though it returns changes in five-minute buckets.

RESOLUTION
Middleware polls the change feed every five minutes and applies updates in order. This is a workaround: updates lag by up to five minutes, polling runs continuously whether or not changes exist, and a missed poll delays a whole bucket. A reviewed inbound path remains the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
Status changes appeared within six minutes across a week of monitoring, and a deliberate poll failure recovered the missed bucket on the following run.

column1: Partner client cannot read structured address fields from the API
column2:
CONTEXT
A partner client reads Account records through the API and needs billing address details.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The partner reports that address information is missing from the responses they receive.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The partner should receive street, city, postal code, and country for each Account.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Their parser ignores the structured address object and reads only top-level fields, so the address arrives empty.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Salesforce returns the address as a compound structure with nested components. The partner client was built against a flat schema and cannot be changed until their next release, which is scheduled for two quarters ahead.

RESOLUTION
Formula fields expose the four address components as top-level values, and the partner reads those. This is a workaround: it duplicates address data into additional fields that must be maintained, and it does not cover other compound fields. Updating the partner client remains the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
The partner retrieved complete addresses for 500 sampled Accounts, and values matched the structured fields exactly.

column1: A small share of callouts returns a success status with an empty body
column2:
CONTEXT
Apex callouts retrieve credit assessments from an external scoring service during opportunity qualification.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
About one call in 500 returns a success status with no payload, leaving the record without a score.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A success response should always contain a scoring payload, or an error status should be returned.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The response carries a success status, a content length of zero, and no error information.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The provider confirmed that their application logged a scoring result for the sampled request identifiers, which suggests the payload is lost between their application and the caller. Retrying the same request immediately succeeds. Requests pass through a corporate egress proxy whose logs are retained for 48 hours and had already rolled over for the first samples.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No retry logic has been added, since silently retrying could hide a genuine provider failure.

VALIDATION
Empty responses continue at a similar rate. The next step is capturing request and response metadata with correlation identifiers on both sides and extending proxy log retention so a failing exchange can be examined.

column1: One of three event subscribers stops receiving a portion of published events
column2:
CONTEXT
Order events published from Apex are consumed by three independent subscribers for billing, analytics, and notifications.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The analytics subscriber is missing roughly one percent of events that the other two receive.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every subscriber should receive the complete event stream published to the channel.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Billing and notification records reconcile with published events, while analytics shows gaps scattered across the day.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Missing events carry no common order type, size, or publishing user. The analytics client reports no errors and its position advances continuously, which means the gaps are not the result of a detected disconnection. A replay of one affected window delivered the missing events successfully, so they were retained and available at the time.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. Replay is used only for investigation and has not been made a standing process.

VALIDATION
Gaps continue at roughly one percent. The next step is logging every received event identifier on the analytics side and comparing it with the published set for a full day, to establish whether events are lost at delivery or discarded after receipt.

column1: Generated queries reference fields the requesting user cannot read
column2:
CONTEXT
An assistant builds SOQL from business questions and runs it in the context of the requesting user.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Support team leads receive an access error instead of an answer for several routine questions.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Generated queries should use only fields the requesting user is permitted to read.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The query includes a restricted margin field, and the platform rejects the whole statement.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The schema description given to the model was exported once from an administrator context and contained every field. Traces showed the model selecting the restricted field when a question mentioned profitability, which was the closest match in the schema text.

RESOLUTION
The schema is now assembled per session from the fields the requesting user can read, and any generated query naming an unavailable field is rejected before execution with an explanation.

VALIDATION
Fifty questions run as three different profiles produced no access errors, restricted users received an explanation instead of a failure, and administrators still reached the full field set.

column1: Assistant builds text searches against fields that cannot be filtered
column2:
CONTEXT
Users ask the assistant to find records containing particular wording in their description.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Questions that search free text fail with a syntax error rather than returning results.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Text searches should run against fields that support filtering, or the assistant should explain the limitation.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The generated query applies a wildcard comparison to a long text area, which the platform does not allow in that position.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The schema description did not record which fields support filtering. Failure traces showed every error involving a long text or rich text field, while searches over standard text fields succeeded.

RESOLUTION
The schema now carries a filterable attribute per field, the generator restricts wildcard comparisons to filterable fields, and text-heavy questions are routed to a search-based path instead.

VALIDATION
A 45-question set produced no syntax errors, searches over long text returned results through the search path, and comparison behavior on standard fields was unchanged.

column1: Quarter-based questions are answered against calendar quarters
column2:
CONTEXT
The organization runs a fiscal year that starts in February, and the assistant answers questions about quarterly performance.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Answers about the current quarter do not match the numbers shown in official reports.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Quarter references should resolve to fiscal quarters as defined by the organization.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The generated query uses calendar quarter boundaries, so results include or exclude a month at each end.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The prompt offered no fiscal definition, so the model used calendar defaults. Comparing eight quarterly questions with official reports showed a consistent one-month shift and differences up to 14 percent in reported revenue.

RESOLUTION
The generator now resolves quarter and year references through fiscal literals defined for the organization, and each answer states the exact period used.

VALIDATION
Eight quarterly questions matched official reports exactly, boundary questions asked on the first and last fiscal day resolved correctly, and the stated period appeared in every answer.

column1: Assistant queries a retired object that is kept only for archive purposes
column2:
CONTEXT
An archived custom object retains historical service records, while current work uses a replacement object.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Answers about service volume are far lower than expected, or mix current and archived data.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Questions about current operations should use the active object only.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The assistant selects the archived object because its name matches the business term more closely.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Both objects remained in the schema description with similar labels and no indication of status. Traces showed the archived object chosen for two thirds of service questions, and its record count stops at the migration date.

RESOLUTION
The schema now carries a lifecycle attribute, retired objects are excluded from generation unless a question explicitly asks for historical data, and the answer names the object used.

VALIDATION
Thirty service questions selected the active object, two explicitly historical questions selected the archive, and reported volumes matched the operational dashboard.

column1: Questions asking for records without related activity return the opposite set
column2:
CONTEXT
Account managers ask the assistant which customers have no open cases or no recent orders.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Answers list customers that clearly do have the related records the question excludes.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A question phrased as an absence should return only parent records with no matching child records.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The generated query filters for the presence of the related records, so the result is the inverse of the request.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The generator had no pattern for expressing absence and produced a straightforward relationship filter. Traces showed the negation words present in the question but absent from the resulting query in 18 of 20 cases.

RESOLUTION
Absence questions are now detected during intent classification and generated with an exclusion subquery, and the answer restates the condition in words so the user can confirm the interpretation.

VALIDATION
Twenty absence questions returned sets that matched manually written queries exactly, and mixed questions combining presence and absence resolved correctly.

column1: Ranking questions sort by a text field instead of a numeric measure
column2:
CONTEXT
Users ask for the largest customers, the highest value deals, or the busiest service areas.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Returned lists are not ordered by size and contain small records at the top.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Ranking questions should order by the relevant numeric measure in descending order.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The query orders by a text field whose label resembles the ranking term, producing alphabetical results.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The schema exposes both a numeric revenue field and a text band field with similar labels. Traces showed the text field selected in 12 of 15 ranking questions, and the resulting order was alphabetical rather than numeric in every case.

RESOLUTION
Ranking intents now require a numeric or aggregate field for ordering, the schema marks measures explicitly, and the generator rejects an ordering clause on a non-numeric field for these questions.

VALIDATION
Fifteen ranking questions ordered correctly by value, results matched manually written queries, and a question deliberately asking for alphabetical order still produced a text ordering.

column1: Queries spanning three related objects fail to resolve the relationship path
column2:
CONTEXT
Some questions require data from three levels, such as case, account, and parent account.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Questions crossing more than two objects either fail or silently drop a condition.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The assistant should traverse valid relationship paths or explain that the path is unsupported.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Three-level paths produce an invalid field name error, or the outermost condition disappears from the query.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The prompt contained direct parent relationships only, so deeper paths were assembled by guesswork. A 30-question set showed 21 failures, all needing at least three levels, and no failure among two-level questions.

RESOLUTION
Validated three-level paths for the eight most common object combinations were added, and unsupported paths now return an explanation. This is partial: deeper paths and less common combinations are still unsupported, and the path list is maintained by hand.

VALIDATION
Nineteen of the 21 previously failing questions now succeed and match manual queries, while two requiring a fourth level return the explanation.

column1: Guardrails block data changes but not expensive unfiltered queries
column2:
CONTEXT
The assistant runs generated statements against production data on behalf of business users.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A broad question produced a query that scanned a very large object and degraded response times for other users.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Generated statements should be prevented from modifying data and from running queries that scan excessive volume.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Data modification is blocked reliably, while an unfiltered query over a large object is accepted and executed.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The guardrail inspected statement type only. A review of a week of traffic found 14 queries with no selective filter, three of which ran for more than a minute, all generated from vague questions.

RESOLUTION
Statement type blocking was retained and a mandatory date or owner filter is now injected when a question has no bounding condition. This is partial: the filter is applied by rule rather than by an actual cost estimate, so an expensive query with a wide date range still runs.

VALIDATION
Data modification remained blocked across 200 generated statements, unfiltered scans fell from 14 to zero in two weeks, and one wide-range query still ran for 40 seconds.

column1: Business terminology must be re-explained by users in every new session
column2:
CONTEXT
Local business terms such as service tier names and regional groupings do not appear in the Salesforce schema.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Users must describe the same terms in every session before the assistant can answer correctly.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Approved business terminology should be available to the assistant without user effort.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Each session starts without any business context, and answers differ depending on how a user explains a term.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
No glossary existed, and terms were passed ad hoc in the question text. Reviewing 40 sessions showed nine terms explained repeatedly, with three explained inconsistently by different users.

RESOLUTION
A curated glossary file listing the nine terms is prepended to every session. This is a workaround: the file is edited manually and reviewed quarterly, so new terminology lags behind the business, and no ownership process exists yet. A maintained dictionary with defined owners is the preferred solution.

VALIDATION
Answers for the nine terms became consistent across users in a 30-question review, while two new terms introduced during the period were still unrecognized.

column1: Answers occasionally correspond to another user's question during busy periods
column2:
CONTEXT
The assistant serves multiple business users concurrently, each in an isolated session.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Two users received an answer that did not match the question they asked.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every answer must correspond to the question asked in that session, using data the user may see.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
During peak periods an answer arrives that appears to belong to another question.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The assistant was restricted to a small pilot group and capped at one request per user during the investigation, and the security team was notified because cross-session content may expose data. Request logs for the reported cases show two requests handled by the same worker within the same second. Scripted parallel questions did not reproduce a mismatch in 500 attempts.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. Containment is in place, but the mechanism is not established and no code change has been released.

VALIDATION
No further reports since the concurrency cap, though the cap also lowers the load needed to trigger the fault. The next step is per-request correlation identifiers through the pipeline and a load test replaying the recorded traffic.

column1: Amounts are inflated a hundredfold for records exported with a comma separator
column2:
CONTEXT
Contract values are migrated from a legacy system whose export follows the regional numeric format.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A group of migrated contracts shows values a hundred times larger than the source.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Migrated amounts should equal the source values exactly.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Values written with a comma as the decimal separator are read as thousands separators, so decimals become whole units.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The export was produced on a workstation with regional settings, while the loader assumed a period separator. Comparing 500 records showed the error only where the source value had a fractional part, which explains why most records looked correct.

RESOLUTION
The export now emits a fixed invariant format, the loader validates the separator before parsing, and a checksum compares the sum of loaded amounts against the source total for each batch.

VALIDATION
The 2,300 affected contracts were corrected and matched the source, the batch checksum passed on three subsequent loads, and a deliberately misformatted file was rejected.

column1: Migrated service records are created under the wrong record type
column2:
CONTEXT
Legacy service records carry a category that determines which Salesforce record type they should use.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Agents cannot find migrated records in their queues, and required fields appear blank on the layout.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each migrated record should adopt the record type matching its legacy category.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Every migrated record uses the default record type, so layout and picklist values do not match its content.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The load file did not include a record type column, so the platform applied the loading user's default. A count by category showed that 62 percent of records should have used one of two other record types.

RESOLUTION
A mapping table translates legacy categories to record types, the load file now includes the resolved value, and affected records were updated in a controlled batch that preserved other field values.

VALIDATION
Record type distribution matched the legacy category distribution exactly after the correction, queue filters returned the expected volumes, and layouts displayed the correct fields.

column1: Migrated notes lose their paragraph structure and become unreadable
column2:
CONTEXT
Free-text case notes are migrated from a legacy system into Salesforce notes linked to the corresponding records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Agents report migrated notes arriving as a single continuous block of text.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Paragraph breaks and list structure present in the source should be preserved.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
All line breaks are removed, and lists run together into one sentence.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The intermediate transformation stripped control characters to avoid breaking the file format, which removed the line break characters together with them. The target content type supports markup, so the structure could be represented if it were preserved.

RESOLUTION
Line breaks are now escaped rather than stripped, converted to markup during load, and a sample comparison runs automatically on each batch.

VALIDATION
Three hundred re-migrated notes matched their source structure, agents confirmed readability in a review of 50 notes, and the automatic comparison flagged a deliberately corrupted test batch.

column1: Repeated migration runs create duplicates instead of updating existing records
column2:
CONTEXT
Customer records are loaded in successive migration waves keyed on a legacy identifier stored in a custom field.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The second wave created new records for customers that the first wave had already loaded.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A record already present should be updated by its legacy identifier rather than duplicated.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Both waves inserted rows, so affected customers exist twice with the same legacy identifier.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The custom field was created without the external identifier and unique attributes, so it could not serve as an upsert key and the load ran as an insert. A query grouping by the identifier found 4,100 duplicate pairs, all created during the second wave.

RESOLUTION
The field was redefined as a unique external identifier, duplicates were merged with the earliest record surviving, and later waves run as upserts on that key.

VALIDATION
A third wave updated existing records with no inserts, the duplicate query returned no rows after the merge, and a deliberate rerun of the same file produced no new records.

column1: List views and reports slow sharply after migrated records land on one owner
column2:
CONTEXT
Three million historical Accounts were migrated and assigned to a single migration user pending owner mapping.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
List views, reports, and searches became noticeably slower after the migration wave completed.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Query performance should remain stable after historical data is loaded.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Queries filtered by owner or run by users in the migration user's role take several times longer than before.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Concentrating records under one owner creates skew in sharing and ownership structures, which makes owner-based filters far less effective. A query plan for an affected report showed a scan cost consistent with the full record set rather than a filtered subset.

RESOLUTION
Records were redistributed to their mapped business owners in batches, unmapped records moved to several queues instead of one user, and no single owner now holds more than a defined share of the object.

VALIDATION
Report runtime returned to pre-migration levels for six sampled reports, the query plan showed selective filtering again, and the largest owner now holds under two percent of records.

column1: Legacy placeholder dates are migrated as real contract dates
column2:
CONTEXT
Legacy contracts use a fixed placeholder date to mean that a value was never entered.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Renewal reports show a cluster of contracts with an implausible historical start date.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Placeholder values should migrate as empty dates rather than as real ones.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The placeholder is a valid date, so it loaded successfully and now appears in reporting and automation.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The mapping copied date fields without inspecting their values. A distribution check found 7,800 contracts sharing the same start date, which is impossible in normal operation, and the same value appeared in two other date fields.

RESOLUTION
The transformation converts the placeholder to an empty value across all date fields, the affected records were corrected, and a distribution check now runs on every migration batch to detect improbable clustering.

VALIDATION
The renewal report no longer shows the cluster, the 7,800 contracts hold empty start dates with a data quality flag, and the distribution check flagged a seeded test file.

column1: Pre-migration deduplication matches only records that carry an email address
column2:
CONTEXT
Contacts from two legacy systems are deduplicated before loading so that each person exists once.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Duplicate people still appear after loading, particularly for older records.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Deduplication should identify the same person across both sources regardless of which attributes are populated.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Matching relies on email, so records without an email address are always treated as distinct.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Around 30 percent of legacy contacts have no email, mostly created before online forms were introduced. A sample of 400 such records showed roughly a quarter were duplicates identifiable by name, phone, and account.

RESOLUTION
A secondary rule now matches on normalized name plus account plus phone, and low confidence matches are routed to a manual review queue. This is partial: records with no email and no phone remain unmatched, and about 900 pairs stay in the review queue awaiting a data steward.

VALIDATION
Duplicate pairs found after load fell from 1,600 to 380 in a rehearsal, and manual review of 100 automatic matches found no incorrect merge.

column1: History for closed legacy accounts cannot be exported from the source system
column2:
CONTEXT
The legacy platform is being retired, and its interaction history must remain available for regulatory review.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Interactions belonging to closed accounts cannot be extracted through the standard export.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
All interaction history should migrate into Salesforce with its original relationships.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The export tool includes active accounts only, and the vendor cannot extend it before the shutdown date.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Closed accounts are archived into a separate database that the export tool does not read. A database-level extract was possible but produced a flat structure without the relationship keys used by the application.

RESOLUTION
The flat extract was loaded into a read-only custom object with search by legacy identifier and date. This is a workaround: those interactions are not linked to Salesforce accounts and cannot be reported alongside migrated history. Reconstructing the relationships requires a key mapping the vendor has not provided.

VALIDATION
Regulatory reviewers retrieved 25 sampled historical interactions by legacy identifier, and record counts matched the archive database exactly.

column1: A subset of records fails reload with an empty error file
column2:
CONTEXT
Migration waves are loaded in batches, and failures are expected to be written to an error file for correction.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Around 200 records per wave are missing after load, but the error file produced for those batches is empty.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every record that fails to load should appear in the error file with a message.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Success counts match the submitted row count, yet the records cannot be found in Salesforce afterwards.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Batch results report success for the missing rows, yet no matching records exist by external identifier or name. The missing rows are not concentrated in one batch or file position, and reloading them individually succeeds, which rules out data content. Storage limits and deletion triggers were checked and excluded.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. Reloading individual records is used for recovery but does not explain the loss.

VALIDATION
The gap recurs at a similar rate in each wave. The next step is capturing the job result payload with record identifiers for a complete wave and querying those identifiers immediately after the job completes.

column1: Some migrated contacts are linked to the wrong account after the final wave
column2:
CONTEXT
Contacts are linked to Accounts during migration through a mapping from legacy customer keys to Salesforce records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Spot checks after the final wave found contacts attached to a different customer in the same corporate group.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each contact should be linked to the account that holds its legacy customer key.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
A subset is linked to a sibling account, which risks correspondence reaching the wrong organization.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Affected contacts were excluded from correspondence and reporting pending review. Every examined case belongs to a corporate group where several accounts share a billing key, but that pattern also holds for correctly linked contacts, so the shared key does not explain the outcome. The mapping file was re-derived and matched the intended assignment for the sampled records.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. The extent is not yet established and no corrective load has been run.

VALIDATION
The error rate in a 500 record sample was 3 percent. The next step is a full comparison of loaded links against the source mapping for the wave, with a per-record mismatch report before any correction.

column1: Entitlement lookup returns an arbitrary record when several are active
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow attaches the correct service entitlement to a new Case by looking up active entitlements on the Account.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Cases for customers holding several contracts are attached to an entitlement that does not match the product purchased.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The flow should select the entitlement covering the Case product with the earliest expiry among valid options.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Whichever entitlement the platform returns first is applied, and the selection changes between otherwise identical Cases.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The Get Records element was configured to store only the first record with no sort order, so the result depended on internal ordering. Accounts with one entitlement were always correct, which is why the defect surfaced only for multi-contract customers.

RESOLUTION
The lookup now filters on the Case product, sorts by expiry date ascending, and a decision handles the case where no entitlement matches by routing to the uncovered support queue.

VALIDATION
Thirty Cases across accounts with one, three, and five entitlements attached the expected record every time, and products with no entitlement routed to the uncovered queue.

column1: Double-clicking submit on a screen flow creates two service requests
column2:
CONTEXT
Agents raise internal service requests through a screen flow that creates a record on the final screen.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Fulfilment teams receive pairs of identical requests submitted seconds apart by the same agent.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
One completed flow run should create exactly one request regardless of how the submit button is pressed.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
A second click before the screen advances starts a second create action, and both records are saved.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The create element ran directly from the submit action with no guard. Paired records shared identical field values and creation times within two seconds, and the pattern was reproduced by clicking twice on a slow connection.

RESOLUTION
The flow now sets a submitted flag in a screen variable and a decision ends the interview if it is already set, while the create element checks for a request raised by the same user for the same asset within the last minute.

VALIDATION
Rapid double and triple clicks produced one record in 40 attempts, and legitimate repeat requests raised more than a minute apart were still created.

column1: Multi-select criteria never match, so escalation branches are skipped
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow escalates Cases whose impact field, a multi-select picklist, includes a regulatory impact value.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Regulatory Cases are never escalated, even when the impact field clearly carries that value.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The escalation branch should run whenever the regulatory value is among the selected impacts.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The branch runs only when the regulatory value is the sole selection, and never when combined with others.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The decision used an equals comparison against the single value, while multi-select fields store selections as a delimited string. Debug logs showed the stored value as a combined string that never equalled the single comparison value.

RESOLUTION
The decision now uses a contains comparison, and a formula normalizes the delimiter before evaluation so ordering of selections does not matter.

VALIDATION
Cases carrying the regulatory value alone and in five different combinations all escalated, while Cases without it were untouched, across 25 test records.

column1: Customers receive two identical status notifications for one update
column2:
CONTEXT
Customers are notified when their Case moves to a resolved state, and the notification is sent by a record-triggered flow.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Customers report receiving the same resolution message twice within a few seconds.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A single status change should produce exactly one customer notification.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Two messages arrive with identical content but different message identifiers.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
A workflow rule created before the flow was still active and sent the same alert. The two automations were built by different teams a year apart, and the older rule was never retired. Message logs showed one send from each automation for every resolved Case.

RESOLUTION
The workflow rule was deactivated and deleted after confirming the flow covered every condition it handled, including a legacy record type the flow had not originally matched.

VALIDATION
Fifty resolutions produced one message each across all record types, and the legacy record type continued to receive a notification through the flow.

column1: Parent update removes child checklist items created by another team
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow maintains onboarding checklist items on a project record and removes items that no longer apply when the project scope changes.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Checklist items created manually by the delivery team disappeared after an unrelated project field was edited.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Cleanup should remove only the generated items that no longer match the current scope.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Every checklist item on the project is deleted and only the generated set is recreated.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The delete element selected all child items for the project rather than filtering on the generated source flag. Record history for three affected projects showed manual items deleted in the same transaction as an unrelated field update, because the flow ran on any project change.

RESOLUTION
The delete now filters on the generated source flag, the flow entry criteria are limited to scope field changes, and manual items are excluded from cleanup entirely.

VALIDATION
Scope changes on 20 projects removed only obsolete generated items, manual items survived, and unrelated field edits triggered no cleanup at all.

column1: Response timers pause correctly for one support calendar only
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow-driven response timer pauses while a Case waits on the customer and resumes when the customer replies.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Timers for the regional support teams do not pause outside their local working hours.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each Case should measure elapsed response time against the working calendar of the team that owns it.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
All Cases are measured against the head office calendar, so overnight waiting time counts against regional teams.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The timer referenced a single hard-coded business hours record. A review of 900 breaches found 340 attributable to hours outside the owning team's working day, concentrated in two regions.

RESOLUTION
The timer now resolves business hours from the owning queue for the two largest regions. This is partial: three smaller regions have no configured calendar yet and still fall back to head office hours, so their breach figures remain overstated.

VALIDATION
Breach counts in the two configured regions fell by 31 percent and matched manual recalculation for a sampled week, while the three remaining regions were unchanged.

column1: Retry handling covers callout failures but not transaction rollbacks
column2:
CONTEXT
A flow sends approved orders to a fulfilment service through an invocable callout and records the response on the order.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Some approved orders never reach fulfilment and show no error on the record.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every approved order should either reach fulfilment or be visibly marked as failed for follow-up.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Orders whose transaction rolls back after the callout are lost, because the failure record is rolled back with them.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Retry logic handles callout errors returned by the service, but a later validation failure in the same transaction discards both the order update and the error log. Comparing fulfilment records with approved orders found 46 gaps in a month, all with a rollback in the debug logs.

RESOLUTION
Failures are now written through a platform event that survives rollback, and a monitor lists orders with no fulfilment acknowledgement. This is partial: the callout itself is not replayed automatically, so recovery is still a manual resubmission.

VALIDATION
All 46 historical gaps were identified by the monitor, and new rollbacks produced a visible failure entry within a minute.

column1: Flow duplicate check cannot use the configured matching rules
column2:
CONTEXT
A screen flow captures new business contacts at events and creates Contact records on the spot.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Staff want the flow to warn them when a contact already exists, using the same logic as the standard duplicate rules.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
The flow should apply the configured matching rules and show the potential duplicates it finds.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The flow cannot invoke the matching engine directly, so it creates records without any duplicate warning.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Matching rules apply automatically to record saves but are not callable from a flow element. A test showed the duplicate rule alert appears only after the create, at which point staff have already left the screen.

RESOLUTION
The flow now runs a query on normalized email and surname before the create and shows any matches. This is a workaround: the query performs exact matching only, so fuzzy variations the standard rules catch are missed, and the rule set must be replicated by hand if it changes.

VALIDATION
Exact duplicates were detected in 48 of 50 test entries, while two records differing by a nickname were created as new contacts.

column1: Case assignment automation has to be disabled by hand during bulk loads
column2:
CONTEXT
Case assignment and notification automation runs on every Case creation, including records loaded during monthly migrations from an acquired business.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Migration loads trigger thousands of assignment notifications and reassign historical Cases to live queues.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Historical loads should create Cases without triggering live operational automation.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The flow cannot distinguish loaded records from genuine new Cases, so every load disrupts the support queues.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The flow has no bypass condition, and the loading account uses the same profile as an administrator. A load of 12,000 Cases produced the same number of queue assignments and notification records.

RESOLUTION
A custom setting now disables the automation while a load runs, toggled manually before and after. This is a workaround: the switch is global, so genuine Cases created during the window are also skipped and must be reprocessed afterwards. A per-user bypass driven by a custom permission is the preferred design.

VALIDATION
Two monthly loads completed with no queue disruption, and the reprocessing job caught 23 genuine Cases created during the windows.

column1: Flow interviews occasionally fail with an error naming a removed element
column2:
CONTEXT
A record-triggered flow on Opportunity has been revised several times, and only the latest version is active.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A handful of interviews each week fail with an error referencing an element that was removed two versions ago.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every interview should run against the active version and its current elements.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Failed interviews name an element that no longer exists, while most interviews on the same records succeed.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The active version was confirmed in setup and in the deployment record. Paused interviews created under older versions complete against the version they started with, but the failing records show no pause element in their path. Deleting and redeploying the flow in a sandbox did not reproduce the error across 2,000 runs.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. The flow has not been rebuilt, because the failure has not been reproduced outside production.

VALIDATION
Failures continue at three to six per week with no pattern by record or user. The next step is exporting the full interview log for a failing record and raising a support case with the flow version history attached.

column1: Middleware reports success while several mapped fields are never written
column2:
CONTEXT
An integration maps 40 fields from the service platform onto Salesforce Case records.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Four fields are always empty in Salesforce although the middleware reports every message as processed.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every mapped field should be written, or the message should fail with a clear error.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Values for those fields are accepted in the request and discarded without any error being returned.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Three of the four targets are formula fields and one is a roll-up summary, none of which accept written values. The API ignores non-writable fields rather than rejecting the request, so the middleware saw a successful response. The mapping had been copied from an older org where those fields were editable.

RESOLUTION
The mapping was corrected to write to the underlying source fields, and a build-time check now compares every mapping target against the object describe and fails the deployment when a target is not writable.

VALIDATION
All 40 fields populated correctly across 500 replayed messages, and a deliberately invalid mapping was rejected by the build check.

column1: Integration keeps updating an account record that no longer exists after a merge
column2:
CONTEXT
The ERP integration stores the Salesforce record key for each customer and uses it for subsequent updates.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Updates for customers merged during data cleansing fail and the ERP marks them as permanently errored.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Updates should follow the surviving record after a merge without manual intervention.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The integration continues to address the losing record key and receives a not-found error on every attempt.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Merges delete the losing record, and the stored key becomes invalid. The middleware had no handling for that error and no awareness of merges. A reconciliation found 260 customers with stale keys, all merged in the previous two cleansing rounds.

RESOLUTION
The integration now resolves records by the external customer identifier rather than the stored key, and a merge event handler updates the middleware mapping when a merge occurs.

VALIDATION
All 260 stale mappings were repaired and their queued updates applied, and a test merge redirected subsequent updates to the surviving record within one cycle.

column1: Scheduled synchronization stops after the client certificate expires
column2:
CONTEXT
A nightly integration authenticates to the partner platform with mutual certificate authentication.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Synchronization stopped for three consecutive nights before anyone noticed the data was stale.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Certificate expiry should be anticipated and replaced before it interrupts the schedule.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The handshake was refused after the certificate expired, and the job logged a connection failure that nobody was watching.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The certificate had a two-year validity and no renewal reminder. The job wrote failures to a log file but raised no alert, so three failed runs passed unnoticed. No credential value was exposed during the investigation.

RESOLUTION
A replacement certificate was installed, an inventory of integration certificates with expiry dates was created, and alerts now fire 60 and 15 days before expiry as well as on any authentication failure.

VALIDATION
The nightly job resumed and cleared the three-day backlog, the expiry alert fired correctly in a test with a short-lived certificate, and a simulated authentication failure raised an immediate alert.

column1: Large customer documents are silently skipped by the document synchronization
column2:
CONTEXT
Documents attached to service requests in the partner system are copied into Salesforce as files on the related Case.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Engineers find Cases without the technical drawings the customer submitted.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every document should transfer, or the failure should be visible on the Case.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Documents above a few megabytes never arrive, and the transfer log records the message as complete.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The middleware sends documents as a single encoded payload, and the platform rejected requests above its size threshold. The handler caught the rejection, logged it at debug level, and continued to the next document. Of 4,300 documents, 190 exceeded the threshold, all engineering drawings.

RESOLUTION
Large documents are now uploaded in chunks and assembled on completion, and any transfer failure creates a visible entry on the Case with a retry action.

VALIDATION
All 190 missing documents transferred with matching checksums, a 45 megabyte test file uploaded successfully, and a forced failure produced the expected Case entry.

column1: Contacts created by the portal integration are invisible in account views
column2:
CONTEXT
A self-service portal creates Contact records in Salesforce when a new user registers.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Account managers cannot see registered users on the account they belong to.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each registered user should appear on the related Account contact list.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The Contact exists and can be found by search, but no Account is linked and the record behaves as a private contact.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The registration payload carries a company identifier that the mapping never used, so the account reference was left empty. A query found 3,900 contacts without an account, all created by the portal integration since it went live.

RESOLUTION
The mapping now resolves the company identifier to an Account and rejects the registration when no match exists, sending the record to a review queue instead of creating an unlinked contact.

VALIDATION
The 3,900 existing contacts were linked by a one-time job using the stored company identifier, 12 unmatched records went to the review queue, and new registrations link correctly.

column1: Product weights arrive in the wrong unit after a supplier schema change
column2:
CONTEXT
Product master data including shipping weight is imported from a supplier feed and used to calculate delivery charges.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Delivery charge estimates for a group of products became implausibly high.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Weights should be stored in kilograms regardless of the unit the supplier uses.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Weights for products from one supplier are a thousand times too large, which inflates every charge calculation.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The supplier changed their feed to report grams and added a unit field the mapping ignored. Comparing 60 products against the printed catalogue confirmed the factor of one thousand, and only that supplier's products were affected.

RESOLUTION
The mapping now reads the unit field, converts to kilograms, and rejects records whose unit is unrecognized so they cannot load with an assumed unit.

VALIDATION
The 1,600 affected products were reloaded and matched the catalogue, delivery estimates returned to expected ranges, and a record with an unknown unit was rejected as designed.

column1: Near real-time synchronization is enabled for strategic accounts only
column2:
CONTEXT
Account and opportunity changes synchronize to the analytics platform on a nightly schedule.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Executive reviews need current figures for strategic accounts during the working day.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Changes on accounts that matter to the review should be visible within minutes.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
All accounts wait for the nightly run, so the morning review works with figures up to a day old.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Event volume for the full account base exceeds the platform's ingestion allowance during business hours. Measurement showed that the 400 strategic accounts generate under four percent of daily change events.

RESOLUTION
Change events are now published for strategic accounts and applied within minutes, while the remainder stay on the nightly schedule. This is partial: the account base is split into two freshness tiers, so any cross-account total mixes current and overnight data unless the whole set is refreshed.

VALIDATION
Strategic account changes appeared within four minutes over two weeks, ingestion stayed within allowance, and mixed-tier totals were labelled with their refresh time.

column1: Integration changes cannot be tested end to end before release
column2:
CONTEXT
Integration changes are developed against a Salesforce sandbox that must connect to the partner platform.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Defects reach production because the partner has no test environment reachable from the sandbox.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every integration change should be exercised against a representative partner environment before release.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Changes are tested against production-shaped assumptions and fail on payload details discovered only after release.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The partner offers no external test instance, and their production network is unreachable from the sandbox by policy. Four of the last seven integration defects came from payload differences that a real exchange would have exposed.

RESOLUTION
A stub service now replays recorded production payloads for regression testing. This is a workaround: recordings age as the partner changes their schema, and the stub cannot reveal behaviour the recordings never captured. A partner test environment remains the stated requirement.

VALIDATION
The stub reproduced three of the four historical defects in regression, while a fifth defect involving a new field was not detected because no recording contained it.

column1: Some updates apply in Salesforce but are never acknowledged to the sender
column2:
CONTEXT
The order platform sends updates to Salesforce and waits for an acknowledgement before marking each message complete.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A small number of messages are resent repeatedly although the update is already visible in Salesforce.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
An applied update should always produce an acknowledgement the sender can record.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The record is updated correctly, the sender receives nothing, and the message is retried until it reaches its attempt limit.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Records for the affected messages show the correct values and a matching modification time, so the write succeeded. The middleware logs an outbound acknowledgement for some of them and nothing for others. Network captures were taken for two days without catching an affected exchange, and the pattern does not follow payload size or message type.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. Retry limits were left unchanged, since suppressing the retries would hide the symptom without explaining it.

VALIDATION
The behaviour continues at roughly one message in 2,000. The next step is correlating middleware, gateway, and platform logs on a shared message identifier and holding captures until an affected exchange is recorded.

column1: Integration throughput halves every few days until the connector is restarted
column2:
CONTEXT
A long-running connector process streams changes from Salesforce into the operational data store.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Processing rate degrades over several days until a restart returns it to normal.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Throughput should remain steady for the life of the process.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The rate falls from roughly 900 records per minute to under 400 over three to five days, then recovers fully after a restart.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Salesforce response times measured from the connector stay flat across the degradation, which points at the connector rather than the platform. Memory use grows steadily between restarts, consistent with an accumulation somewhere in the process, but heap analysis on the vendor build was not possible without their debug package. Message volume and payload sizes are unchanged.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. A scheduled restart was considered and not implemented, since it would mask the underlying growth.

VALIDATION
The degradation repeats on the same cycle. The next step is obtaining the vendor debug build, capturing heap snapshots at one, three, and five days, and comparing object retention across them.

column1: Dashboard viewers see figures from a privileged running user
column2:
CONTEXT
A regional performance dashboard is shared with all sales staff through a public folder.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A representative noticed totals covering regions they have no access to in the underlying reports.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each viewer should see only the data their own access permits.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Every viewer sees the same figures, calculated with the access of the dashboard running user.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The dashboard was unshared immediately while the review ran, and the security team was informed. It was configured with a fixed running user holding a broad role, which is how the component figures were produced. Only aggregate values were exposed, since drilling into a component still applied the viewer's own access.

RESOLUTION
The dashboard was converted to run as the viewing user, with a separate leadership dashboard retained for roles entitled to the wider view, and dashboards with fixed running users are now reviewed each release.

VALIDATION
Three representatives from different regions saw only their own figures, leadership retained the full view, and the release review listed every remaining fixed running user.

column1: A custom object left at public read exposes internal supplier terms
column2:
CONTEXT
A supplier agreement object was created during a pilot and later populated with commercial terms.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A procurement review found that all internal users could open supplier pricing records.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Supplier agreements should be visible only to the procurement team and named approvers.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The organization-wide default remained public read from the pilot, so every internal user had read access.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Access was tightened the same day and the security team was notified. The pilot had used a permissive default for convenience, and the go-live checklist did not include a sharing review. Login and report access history showed the object had been opened by 14 users outside procurement, all in browsing patterns rather than bulk extraction.

RESOLUTION
The default was set to private with a sharing rule for the procurement group and a criteria-based rule for approvers, and the go-live checklist now requires an explicit sharing decision per object.

VALIDATION
Users outside procurement received no results for the object in reports and search, procurement retained full access, and the checklist blocked a later object with an unset default.

column1: Self-registered community users receive more access than intended
column2:
CONTEXT
Customers can self-register on the support community, and the registration process assigns a profile and permission set.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A new registration was found to expose the full knowledge base, including internal-only articles.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Self-registered users should reach public articles and their own cases only.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The assigned permission set grants access to all article types, including those marked for internal channels.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Self-registration was suspended and existing accounts were reviewed while the fix was prepared, with the security team informed. The permission set had been cloned from an internal support template and retained its article type access. Article view history showed three internal articles opened by two external users.

RESOLUTION
A dedicated permission set was built from an empty baseline granting only public article types and case access, and the two users were contacted by support to confirm what they had seen.

VALIDATION
A newly registered test user could reach public articles only, internal types returned no results in community search, and the article history review found no further external access.

column1: A formula field reveals the value of a restricted source field
column2:
CONTEXT
Salary band information on the employee object is restricted to the human resources profile through field-level security.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A manager outside human resources was able to infer exact salary bands from a compensation ratio field.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Restricted values must not be readable directly or through derived fields.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
A formula field referencing the restricted field is visible to managers and returns a value derived from it.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The formula field was hidden from the affected profiles and the security team was notified. Field-level security applies to the field being read, not to the fields a formula references, so the restriction was bypassed by design rather than by misconfiguration. Two other formula fields referencing restricted sources were found in the same review.

RESOLUTION
The three formula fields were restricted to the human resources profile, the ratio was replaced with a coarse band that cannot be inverted, and a metadata check now reports formulas referencing restricted fields.

VALIDATION
Managers saw the coarse band only, the restricted values were unreadable through every field on the layout, and the metadata check flagged a test formula added afterwards.

column1: Report data can still be extracted after the export permission was removed
column2:
CONTEXT
The export permission was removed from standard profiles to reduce the risk of bulk data leaving the platform.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A control test showed that users without the permission could still obtain full report data.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Users without the export permission should not be able to extract report contents in bulk.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The printable view renders every row in the browser, from where the content is copied into a spreadsheet.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The export permission governs the export action only, and the printable view is a separate capability. Testing with three profiles confirmed the printable view was available to all of them, and report run history showed regular use of it by two teams.

RESOLUTION
The printable view was disabled for the affected profiles, row limits were applied to the shared report folders, and the two teams received a supported extract for their genuine reporting need.

VALIDATION
The printable view returned no option for the tested profiles, the supported extract met both teams' requirements, and a repeat control test found no remaining bulk path.

column1: Data classification is complete for customer objects but not for operational ones
column2:
CONTEXT
Fields are classified by sensitivity so that access reviews and export controls can be driven from metadata.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The privacy team cannot report on where sensitive data resides because classification is incomplete.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every field holding personal or commercially sensitive data should carry a classification value.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Customer-facing objects are classified, while operational and custom integration objects are largely unclassified.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
A metadata extract found 2,400 fields in total, of which 1,450 carry a classification. The unclassified remainder is concentrated in 40 custom objects, many built by project teams without a data owner recorded.

RESOLUTION
Classification was completed for all customer objects and is now mandatory for new fields through a deployment check. This is partial: the 950 unclassified fields on existing operational objects need a data owner before they can be classified, and 11 objects still have none assigned.

VALIDATION
The privacy report covers all customer objects accurately, the deployment check rejected two unclassified new fields, and the operational gap is tracked with named owners for 29 of 40 objects.

column1: Access reviews are automated for staff but still manual for integration accounts
column2:
CONTEXT
Quarterly access reviews confirm that privileged permissions remain justified.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The review process is slow and evidence for integration accounts is assembled by hand each quarter.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Every privileged account should be reviewed from generated evidence with a recorded decision.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Staff accounts are covered by a generated report, while integration accounts require manual collection from several sources.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Integration accounts hold permissions through permission set groups, connected app policies, and named credential configuration, and only the first is included in the generated report. The last review took nine working days, of which six were spent on 23 integration accounts.

RESOLUTION
The generated evidence now includes permission set groups and profile permissions for all account types. This is partial: connected app policies and named credential scope are still gathered manually, since no report exposes them together.

VALIDATION
Review effort fell to four working days, staff account evidence was complete, and integration accounts still required manual collection for two of the four evidence sources.

column1: A legacy profile cannot be retired because a managed package depends on it
column2:
CONTEXT
A consolidation project is replacing profiles with a small set of baseline profiles and permission sets.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
One legacy profile with broad permissions cannot be removed, which keeps an over-privileged profile in use.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
All users should sit on a baseline profile with additional access granted through permission sets.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
A managed package validates the profile name at runtime and stops working for users moved off it.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The package checks the profile name rather than a permission, which the vendor confirmed. Testing showed 14 of the profile's 60 permissions are required by the package, while the rest are historical.

RESOLUTION
The 46 unnecessary permissions were removed from the profile and the affected users were restricted by a session policy. This is a workaround: the profile survives with more permissions than the baseline, and consolidation cannot complete until the vendor releases a permission-based check.

VALIDATION
The package continued to work for all 30 users after the permissions were stripped, and an access review confirmed the profile now grants 14 permissions instead of 60.

column1: Several users report password reset messages they did not request
column2:
CONTEXT
Password reset messages are sent when a user or an administrator initiates a reset.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Six users received reset messages within an hour, none of whom had requested one.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
A reset message should exist only where a legitimate request was made.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Messages were issued for six accounts with no corresponding administrator action recorded.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Multi-factor authentication was confirmed active on the six accounts, sessions were revoked, logins were restricted to corporate addresses, and the security team opened an incident. Login history shows failed attempts from unfamiliar addresses shortly before each message, consistent with resets requested through the login page using known usernames. The source of those usernames is not established.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause exists. Containment is in place, but the origin of the requests is unconfirmed and no conclusion has been reached about how the usernames were obtained.

VALIDATION
Session records show no access by an unauthorized party, and no further messages have appeared since the restriction. The next step is a review of username exposure with the identity team and correlation with external breach notifications.

column1: Encrypted values appear in clear text in one profile's report exports
column2:
CONTEXT
Bank account fields on the payment object are protected so only finance operations can read them.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
A user outside finance produced a report export in which the values were readable.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Protected values must remain masked for any user not permitted to read them.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The values are masked in the record view for that profile but appear unmasked in one report export.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The report and its folder were withdrawn, the export was recalled, permission to read masked data was audited across all profiles, and the security team opened an incident. The profile does not hold that permission, and the same report exported by a second user on it produced masked values, so the behaviour has not been reproduced.

RESOLUTION
No verified cause or fix exists. No encryption or permission setting has been changed, because the conditions that produced the export are unknown.

VALIDATION
Repeat exports by four users on that profile returned masked values. The next step is a vendor support case with the original export, the report definition, and the user's permission snapshot from the time of the export.

column1: Coverage report omits accounts that have never been contacted
column2:
CONTEXT
A coverage report shows how many accounts in each territory have had a customer interaction this quarter.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
Territory managers say the report cannot be used to find neglected accounts, which is its main purpose.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Accounts with no interactions should appear with a zero so that gaps are visible.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Only accounts with at least one activity are listed, so the very accounts the managers need are absent.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
The report was built on a type that requires a related activity, which excludes unmatched parents. Comparing the report against the account base showed 1,240 accounts missing, all with no activity in the period.

RESOLUTION
The report was rebuilt on a type that includes accounts with or without activities, and the interaction count is presented as zero where none exist.

VALIDATION
Territory totals matched the account base exactly for four territories, the 1,240 previously hidden accounts appeared with zero counts, and accounts with activity kept their original figures.

column1: Regional grouping splits into separate rows for the same region
column2:
CONTEXT
A revenue summary groups accounts by a free-text region field populated by several teams over the years.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
The summary shows the same region several times with the revenue divided between the rows.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Each region should appear once with its complete revenue.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
Values differing only in capitalization or trailing spaces are treated as distinct groups.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
Grouping compares stored values exactly, so variants create separate rows. A distinct value query returned 31 values covering seven actual regions, including entries differing only by a trailing space.

RESOLUTION
The values were normalized to a restricted picklist of seven regions, historical records were mapped in a controlled update, and the field is no longer free text.

VALIDATION
The summary now returns seven rows whose total matches the unfiltered revenue figure, and a distinct value query confirms no variants remain.

column1: Dashboard filter leaves one component showing unfiltered totals
column2:
CONTEXT
A service dashboard carries a filter that restricts every component to a selected business unit.

ISSUE OR REQUEST
One component shows a far higher figure than the others whenever a business unit is selected.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
Selecting a business unit should restrict every component on the dashboard.

ACTUAL BEHAVIOR
The escalation component keeps showing organization-wide totals while the rest respond to the filter.

INVESTIGATION AND FINDINGS
A dashboard filter applies only to components whose source report contains the filter field. The escalation report was built on a report type without the business unit field, so the filter silently skipped it. Selecting each business unit in turn always returned the same escalation figure.

RESOLUTION
The escalation report was rebuilt on a type that exposes the business unit field, and a documented check confirms filter coverage for every component before a dashboard is published.

VALIDATION
Each business unit selection changed all seven components, the escalation figures summed to the organization-wide total, and the coverage check flagged a test component built without the field.

column1: Status filter returns no rows because it uses the displayed label
column2:
CONTEXT
